items.name: Europa
items.desc: The land of … is home to a huge variety of people. With so many cultures, religions, languages, and lifestyles living side by side, … has seen its share of neighborly conflicts as well as cultural synthesis and cooperation. The idea of such a diverse population working towards a single goal seems highly improbable. However, if all the different groups in … united under a single banner and identity, we would achieve nearly unprecedented global power.

items.desc: Not since the second century has one empire commanded the entirety of the Mediterranean and beyond, and that empire was mighty Rome. If we claim this land, we can scoff at whatever pretenders may claim in Constantinople or the Holy Roman Empire, and proclaim ourselves as the true successors of the Roman Empire. Cives Romani sumus!

adv.d: Through carefully laid stone channels and gravity-fed conduits, this construct secures a steady supply of fresh water. While simple in construction, these works mark the first step toward organized urban water management.
The Early Legionaries uphold the oldest traditions of drill and discipline. Spears, broad shields, and firm cohesion let them stand fast even as the battle twists around them.

Peace under Rome does not mean the absence of war, but the triumph of order. Through enforcing our laws and building extensive road systems, as well as the might of our armies, we will bring stability and prosperity to every corner of the Empire.

The Senate and the people of Rome are the eternal foundations of our state. By invoking this ancient authority, we remind all that Rome rules not merely by force of arms, but by the will of its citizens and its institutions.

The growth of our urban centers has created an increasing demand for reliable fresh water. If our towns and cities are to flourish, we must commit to greater feats of engineering and expand our aqueduct networks.
Legionaries trained in the refined arts of close combat, carrying throwing spears and short swords. Their strength lies in steady formations and a military culture of relentless practice.

The Legions were once the pride of Rome, feared and respected across the world. To restore them is to also revive the discipline, organization, and indomitable spirit that our great empire is built upon.
Rome was as much a center of culture as it was an Empire of conquest. By sponsoring poets, scholars, and architects, we will rekindle the creative flame that once illuminated the ancient world.
Our jurists shall compile and refine our laws into a comprehensive body, drawing on the wisdom of Justinian and the Republic alike. In doing so, we will assure justice for all Roman citizens.

The people must be kept happy and sated, for discontent breeds revolt. By putting grain on their tables and providing diverting activities such as games and public festivals, we shall win their loyalty and strengthen the state through their patriotism.
The Reformed Legionaries are hardened infantrymen, equipped with the best armor and weapons, who form the core of our armies.
The Roman road system is the envy of the world. It binds our empire together, speeding merchants, messengers, and soldiers alike, with all paths converging in the Eternal City.

The Heavy Legionaries are elite infantrymen, equipped with the finest armor and weapons. Like the heavy armored legions of ancient Rome, these troops will be the hammer with which we will smite our enemies.

Citizenship is the lifeblood of Rome, binding peoples of every province into a single political body. Extending these rights ensures integration and the promise of advancement for all who serve the empire.

The Guard Legionaries embody the highest standard of soldiering within the legions. Selected from the finest cohorts, they are trusted with critical missions and the protection of the state's highest institutions.
Rome's destiny knows no bounds. From the Pillars of Hercules to the edges of the earth, we will expand our dominion without end, bringing civilization wherever the Imperial Eagle soars.

Our more remote provinces cannot effectively be ruled from Rome only. By placing competent governors in the outlying regions, we will guarantee that our laws are followed and taxes paid promptly in even the most distant lands of the empire.

A triumph is more than a mere procession. Indeed, it is the living memory of conquest, paraded through the streets of our greatest cities. Such ceremonies inspire loyalty, awe, fear, and ambition in equal measure.
These Imperial Legionaries stand at the apex of centuries of military evolution. Masters of equipment and doctrine alike, they serve the lifeguard whose presence alone can steady wavering lines.
From aqueducts to amphitheaters, Roman engineering leaves behind monuments that endure for centuries. Our mastery of stone and arch will show the entire world that Rome's greatness is eternal.

items.name: America
items.desc: We the people are exhausted: by foreign rulers who see us as property, by oppressive and abusive taxation policies when we ourselves have no say in our government, and by the cruelty of our Loyalist neighbors. Long have these colonies been subject to the greed of European powers, but no more! The surge of liberty in the colonies has granted us an opportunity to form a proud federation of independent states free from tyranny. Give us liberty, or give us death!

adv.d: Elected assemblies emerged throughout the colonies, empowering landowners to govern themselves. The humble origins of liberty lie in the halls of these institutions.
Bound together by shared peril and purpose, the early settlers drafted a pact of self-governance. Even in the wilderness, the seeds of society and compromise found soil.
A wave of religious revival sweeps the land, challenging old authorities and stirring the moral conscience of a rising people.
...or abridging the freedom of speech, or of the press; or the right of the people peaceably to assemble, and to petition the Government for a redress of grievances.
We hold these truths to be self-evident, that all men are created equal. With this bold declaration, we shall break the chains of subjugation, and embraced our shared destiny!
Treaties and diplomacy affirmed what our struggles have earned. Our place on the stage of diplomacy is no longer questioned, but respected.
In the wake of hardship, peace and unity have brought a rare moment of national harmony. The people flourish with optimism and order.

items.desc: The glorious Byzantine Empire is long gone, but as long as Greeks live in …, there is hope of its resurrection. Like a phoenix swirling back to life from a pile of ashes, so too must the remnants of Eastern Rome. But before we can reunite into a vital empire, we must quell internal dissent and ensure we are all working towards the same goal. After all, we can take the place of the Byzantine Empire in spirit, but we cannot take its name until we prove worthy of it...

adv.d: Primarily focused on border defense, these light troops are also given lands to farm as well as protect. Akritai are most adept at defensive warfare, especially against cavalry, and are often the first response against external threats.

Through carefully laid stone channels and gravity-fed conduits, this construct secures a steady supply of fresh water. While simple in construction, these works mark the first step toward organized urban water management.
Our administration heaves under the weight of our complex web of bureaucracies, a legacy of centuries of imperial rule.

Our people stand on the shoulders of giants; it is our responsibility to leave comprehensive records of our empire's glory to inspire and instruct future generations. By thoroughly documenting the lives of our extraordinary ancestors, tracing our prestigious lineages, and detailing our intricate traditions, we will surpass mere historical records and become truly legendary.

Constantinople is the beating heart of vibrant faith. We take great pride in being the home of Orthodoxy, holders of the Ecumenical Patriarchate, and defenders of Christendom against our heathen enemies.

Although warfare has evolved significantly since the first incarnation of our empire, including the introduction of gunpowder, the battle tactics refined by our forebears centuries ago are often still effective. Our cataphracts shall embody the best of both our ancient and modern combat wisdom.

The court of Constantinople attracts diplomats and dignitaries from every corner of the known world. As a result, we ensure all languages receive equal respect and accommodation — a practical necessity for an empire at the crossroads of civilizations.
The Varangians have served our country for centuries with distinguished honor and unwavering faith. By expanding their ranks, we will further secure the stability and protection of Byzantium.

The growth of our urban centers has created an increasing demand for reliable fresh water. If our towns and cities are to flourish, we must commit to greater feats of engineering and expand our aqueduct networks.

It is no secret that other nations envy our literary accomplishments and enlightened past. They seek to hire tutors from our court, eager to sink their claws into the knowledge that gave rise to powerful empires and carved the cultural landscape of the entire continent. It is through these men of letters that our neighbors will come to fall in love with our history and become educated in our ways.

Byzantine culture has taken Europe by storm, particularly poikilia — our unique aesthetic. Emphasizing visual variety and a dizzying array of vibrant hues, poikilia creates a symphony of colors and elements in our art and architecture alike.

Powerful warriors that originally hailed from the northern Viking lands, these select few ferocious soldiers make up the core of the royal guard. Armed with axes and shields, they have often been described as pelekyphóroi bárbaroi, axe-wielding barbarians.

We stand between Europe and a sea of heathens, a shield against foreign threats. Our sword will forever be raised against those who seek to eradicate our faith, ready to strike against any who disrespect our traditions.

Byzantium is located between Europe and Asia, making it in many ways the connection between East and West. Our advantageous position is highly lucrative, and has also allowed us to significantly expand our maritime influence.

Europe is engulfed in religious turmoil. We must be prepared to rip up noxious weeds of heresy that appear in the garden of our Empire, lest it become overgrown with heathens. Our pious defense against heretic incursion will prevent us from sinking into instability.

Bureaucracy is a nightmarish endeavor for a country our size. To better refine the religious proceedings required every time we call the Orthodox Synod, we will cut down on the red tape, and revisit the associated legislation.
We are already familiar with deploying and refining powerful siege engines. However, by adapting our designs to use gunpowder, we will be able to completely dominate our foes with our cannons.
Our great nation is the undisputed heir to the splendor and prestige of Rome, and reclaiming that long-lost territory is our primary motivation.

The Strategikon — the ancient manual of cavalry tactics, logistics, and battlefield doctrine — has served us well in times of war. However, as war changes, so must we. Our tactics and regiments have adapted to modern combat, employing weapons of such destruction that Maurice himself could never have anticipated their devastation.

The rediscovery and revival of ancient Greek arts has provided us with a wonderful opportunity to better educate the masses and to preserve our lofty scientific and cultural ideals. We shall make a diligent study of the wisdom of our ancestors.

Our army has lagged behind others in Europe for far too long. By enacting sweeping military reform and expanding our conscription efforts, we hope to build a modern army befitting the resurgent and resplendent phoenix that symbolizes our empire.

items.name: Carthage
items.desc: The foul dogs of the Roman Empire burned the Carthaginian homeland to the ground, trying to erase every single memory of this ancient civilization. Gone may be their identity, culture and religion, but as long as a single Roman pretender exists, so does the need for a foil to these charlatans. We shall become the scourge to all those fools who glorify the Romans; we shall become the Heirs of Carthage!

adv.d: The Phoenician trade fleets of Tyre, Sidon, and Carthage knit the Mediterranean into a single commercial system for half a millennium, and the silver shekels of Cartagena paid the Iberian, Numidian, and Balearic mercenary captains who fought our wars under Hamilcar and Hannibal. Our maritime law inherits the customs of the Punic admirals, our recruiting agents follow the same captains' itineraries through the western Mediterranean, and our paymasters draw on the same model of cash-for-service that spared Punic citizens from the battlefield. This combined commercial-mercenary inheritance gives the restored Carthage both a merchant capacity and a paid-army economy that no younger trading nation can replicate from scratch.

The ancient cothon of Carthage was a circular military harbor with two hundred and twenty sheltered berths, dry-docks, and a central island for the admiral's command, capable of fitting out a full fleet in days while remaining invisible from the open sea. Our shipwrights are reconstructing this same engineering on the harbor floor, drawing the Phoenician diaspora of Gadir, Lixus, Mogador, and Tharros back to the home cities to crew the hulls as they leave the slipways. This restored cothon infrastructure gives Carthage both the shipbuilding tempo and the sailor pool that no rectangular European arsenal can match.

Hannon the Navigator sailed beyond the Pillars of Hercules in the fifth century before Christ, founding seven trading posts along the Atlantic coast of West Africa and pushing south past the limits of all subsequent classical voyaging. His periplus survives in Greek translation and still describes harbors, river mouths, and offshore landmarks that our captains can verify on every voyage south. This documented blue-water tradition gives our Carthaginian explorers a route-book and a logistical template that no European nation can claim to inherit from antiquity.

The ancient Punic colonies at Gadir, Lixus, and Mogador stretched our reach a thousand miles beyond the Pillars of Hercules, and our modern Carthaginian commerce now reaches across every sea opened by the great voyages. Our agents staff the emporia of Asia and the Americas, our convoys carry oil, wine, and manufactures to every navigable port, and our brokers settle bills in every major exchange from London to Goa. This planetary commercial reach gives Carthage both a colonial sailing range and an export network that the Phoenician founders of our line could scarcely have imagined.

Ancient Carthage was governed by two annually-elected Šūfeṭīm (sufetes) drawn from the great merchant families and accountable to a senate of three hundred and a popular assembly. Our restoration of this dual-magistrate constitution combines the proven stability of the Punic model with the legal innovations of the modern republican age. This deep republican lineage gives Carthage a constitutional legitimacy that no upstart Italian or Dutch republic can match for antiquity.

The hinterland of Carthage (the fertile plain of the Medjerda, the slopes of Cape Bon, and the olive groves of the Sahel) earned our region the title of horreum imperii under Roman rule, supplying a third of the imperial grain dole, the bulk of its olive oil, and the cheap amphorae wines that Roman commentators sneered at but bought by the shipload anyway. Our agricultural treatises by Mago the Carthaginian taught the Roman estates how to graft fig trees, press olives, and train drought-resistant vines at industrial scale, and the great rural villas of antiquity now form the foundations of our new mechanized presses, threshing yards, and wine cellars. This Punic-Roman agricultural inheritance, restored under modern industrial conditions, gives Carthage olive and Wine yields that no fresh plantation in the Mediterranean basin can match.

items.name: China

c.t: Situation is active: Red Turban Rebellions

items.desc: The Middle Kingdom refers to China, considered the cultural center of Far East Asia since Antiquity, and therefore in the center — or middle — of the world.

adv.d: Our domain stretches well beyond the horizon. The emergence of a common written language among our subjects will surely bridge the gaps between us, elevate our culture, and reduce conflict based on misunderstanding and linguistic differences.

b: Head of the Cabinet Promotion Cost Modifier: -33%
adv.d: If we are to manage our realm properly, our advisors shall find great wisdom about administration in Confucian teachings, which emphasize meritocratic selection of officials, attention to administrative detail, and other foundational advice for creating a healthy and prosperous government.

Our realm rests upon a tradition of sophisticated administrative institutions, from the Central Secretariat that coordinates all civil governance to the Censorate that holds our officials to account. We shall make this legacy of imperial administration the foundation of our state.
From the days of total conquest to the vast expanses of Genghis Khān's great Empire, our people descend from generations of earthshakers. Our people are the ones destined to author history.
Typically consisting of four acts, this brilliant display of dance and music is a colorful expression of the artistic heights that our society has achieved.

The many rivers that cross our domain have tremendous economic potential. By constructing extensive canal networks, we can connect waterways to inland settlements, making transportation easier while also providing a reliable water supply to our people.

Maintaining control over our territories, policymaking, and military operations is vital for the continuation of our dynasty. Through the creation of Grand Coordinators, a body of high-ranking officials who can coordinate governance across our vast empire, we will succeed in cementing our position through effective stabilization of internal and external matters.

Under the Lǐ Jiǎ system, we are able to exercise control over our borderlands through the allocation of settled armies. By granting land and agricultural rights to our stationed troops, our borders will be safer and our authority shall be affirmed.

A system of subjugated local warlords and other rulers who send us regular gifts of allegiance in recognition of our overlordship. To refine and centralize this system would help us tighten our grip and squeeze more out of them.

Many would-be conquerors eye our lands with covetous intent. If we are to defend our territory, we must set up a garrison system, aimed at rapidly responding to hostile invasions. Through the recruitment of local troops, our defensive prowess will be supplemented through supplies and more efficient logistics.

Tax evasion is a timeless problem that even plagued our ancestors, but we may have found a solution: By compiling registers for districts and provinces, we will keep better track of the taxes owed to the central government by every plot. This taxation is largely determined based on the grain yield of every plot that undergoes survey.
One of the most vital branches of the Three Departments and Six Ministries, the central secretariat is responsible for the drafting and codification of many Imperial reforms and decrees.
The Salt monopoly was once our most important revenue source, but previous Emperors abolished it to encourage free trade. It is time to return the Salt trade to state control.

Parallel to other institutes within our administration, this branch of our government is in charge of preventing corruption. The censors are tasked with keeping palatial intrigues and malfeasance in check, often seen as the eyes and ears of the Emperor.

A staple beverage of our society, Tea has come to dominate social gatherings, becoming the choice drink of many. This will undoubtedly lead to not only new varieties being cultivated, but a production boom as well.

In our quest to shore up our border defenses, it has become apparent that we must create a system of recruitment centered around local soldiers and stalwarts. These fighters will be a valuable addition to our military capabilities, and shall be kept separate from the Wèi Suǒ system.
Titles granted to warlords and local strongmen, these administrative positions are used to quell unrest and keep the rural populace under central control.

Our illustrious military history of our people is a great source of inspiration and pride for our people. By conducting elaborate parades to showcase our armies, we will decisively demonstrate our martial experience and unparalleled strength.

adv.n: Nine Garrisons of the Great Wall
adv.d: In order to defend against the vicious barbarian onslaught, we must do more than simply repair the Great Wall. The Nine Garrisons are militarized garrison towns along the Wall that will not only help to defend the most important passes, but also improve the overall logistical situation on our northern border.

Considered the de facto highest institution in our nation, the … has served our rulers for centuries. Wielding immense influence over administrative affairs, this body of cabinet ministers must undergo a reform to further increase its effectiveness.

By turning most obligations towards the central government - from poll taxes to the labor obligations of the peasants or the tributes of local officials - into a single silver payment, the amount of which is based on the population and cultivated land in each prefecture, tax collection will become easier and our income will increase.

The red-haired barbarians from Europe may be uncivilized and ill-mannered, but they do know how to make artillery and firearms of good quality. Importing and duplicating their weapons will give our army a significant advantage against all invaders.

Our wealthy nation has ample coin and bounteous, fertile fields, but all this abundance requires comprehensive taxation. The Great Tax Reform enables more efficient revenue management, which should guarantee a healthier budget for our realm.

The Green Standard Army, a military force mainly composed of ethnic Hàn soldiers, coexists with our Eight Banner armies. Originally formed by surrendered troops and recruited on a voluntary, long-term basis, they attract individuals from socially disadvantaged backgrounds. Used as a police force post-consolidation, they will play a crucial role in local military governance, while Bannermen will be reserved for emergencies and sustained resistance.

Also known as the Grand Council, the Jūnjī Chù is tasked with overseeing military affairs. As the most important privy council, it has come to overshadow the Grand Secretariat that held sway over previous dynasties. Despite its crucial role, this council will retain an informal nature within the inner court, with its members holding other official roles besides their councilorship.

Our Porcelain industry is emblematic of the prosperity and tradition of artisanal excellence alive in our Empire. By perfecting the already-superior Porcelain production techniques of Jǐngdézhèn, we will spread our cultural influence far and wide.

The production of elegant illustrations, artworks, and books using this printing method has captivated our people's attention, and our master printers constantly strive to perfect their techniques. Woodblock printing has become part of our culture and, with recent improvements to and expansion of our literary production, will further elevate our prestige.

In our people's many millennia of existence on this planet, they have endured thousands of catastrophes through sheer tenacity. This innate steely strength has come to be recognized as a defining feature of our society. We showcase our resilience in the strength of our army and the divine beauty of our art.

The Hall of Three Rarities is our most splendid repository of rare, valuable objects and works of art. Through the generous patronage of our ruler, it has flowered into a venue for academic discussions, lectures, and even cultural events, promoting intellectual exchange and scholarly pursuits.

req: March to the Sound of Guns
adv.d: The Ten Great Campaigns are aimed at expanding our influence both inside and outside our borders. To achieve that, we will draft a huge army to crush any resistance that we might find in our way. We shall choke the life out of any rebellion before it has the chance to raise its head, and our glory will be eternal.

items.name: Germany
items.desc: Despite the absence of a strong central authority, our nation is prospering. The wealthy Hanseatic League, formed by hundreds of towns in northern Germany, has made our nation incredibly prosperous. Intellectual growth, combined with sea and overland trading, has also helped spur development and transform our country into a wealthy hub of manufacturing and intellectual innovation.

adv.d: Since Roman times, road networks have connected places across Germany, making trade and travel easier and more accessible. These roads also provide critical logistical advantages, particularly when moving troops.

Imperial fairs are a rare privilege granted to only a few select cities, creating some of the largest marketplaces in Europe and making these cities the commercial heart of the Holy Roman Empire. The centralized nature of these markets allows merchants to plan and negotiate effectively in a setting where they can benefit from freedom and access to a diverse variety of goods.

The Biedermeier period marks a shift in social conservatism stemming from the upper classes and their nostalgia for the time when they held the most influence and power in our country. This social change has led our more free-thinking citizens to shroud their creative and intellectual pursuits in relative secrecy, well out of the public's disapproving gaze. While this inadvertently strengthens the development of a cultural identity amongst our merchants, it has also forced many valuable minds to leave our nation, seeking their lost freedoms — and taking their talents — elsewhere.

items.name: Hindustan
items.desc: People from India, although highly diverse in culture, traditions, and beliefs, all belong to this same land, and share its history. Therefore, we must put aside these differences and work towards a common goal of establishing a strong Hindustan state, presenting ourselves as a unified people against any who might oppose us.

adv.d: Neglecting the importance of the infantry has been the downfall of many would-be conquerors. We must ensure that our troops are equipped with the most effective firearms and drilled in tactics that can adapt to any foe.

The many people, cultures, languages, and nations that make up India shall be finally united under a single banner. Only with common understanding and a carefully fostered unity among all our people can we strive towards greater ambitions.

Many Hindu faithful worship the river Ganges as a goddess that brings purity and redemption to the faithful. We implore pilgrims to visit the river banks to bathe in the sacred waters. Through Gaṅgā, our nation is made pure.
Foreign languages and noble customs have richly influenced the courts of India for a long time. We should utilize these connections to invite the most capable advisors to serve under our guidance.

b: Invite Religious Figure from Same School Cost: -50%
adv.d: Muslim princes across the world compete to attract the wisest Sufi teachers. As our renown has grown, more of these Sufis have joined us. Towns are founded wherever they settle, often in previously inhospitable regions, and the local people are inspired to convert through the wisdom of the Sufis.
Our mastery of gunpowder warfare has brought us glory and helped us found our great state. This dominance would be impossible without fostering firearms production for our troops.
No ruler, be they Muslim, Hindu, Buddhist, or Jain, has ever succeeded in conquering the entirety of the subcontinent. We shall be the first universal rulers of India!

Governing a state as large as an entire subcontinent is no easy task. We will need to develop a robust system of administration in cooperation with local princes to get the most out of our production and to ensure widespread stability.

Iron-cased rockets have yet to be widely adapted for military purposes, yet their explosive power surely has tactical applications. We should experiment with this technology and test it on the battlefield.

Conditions in our economy are ideal for rapid industrial growth. With new technology we can ensure better conditions for our local production, particularly in the textile industry. Our focus on new methods means that our state can ensure steady industrial expansion.

items.name: Holy Rome

pot.t: Member of organization: Holy Roman Empire

allow.t: The Holy Roman Empire can only be formed via the … … of the …

items.desc: The glory of the ancient Roman Empire lives in the memory of all in …. … was crowned Roman Emperor, but it was not until the coronation of … that the current Holy Roman Empire was born, with the ambitions of forming a revived and unified European Empire.

items.name: Italy

c.t: We won Guelphs and Ghibellines Situation as the leader of the Guelphs

items.desc: As the heart of the Renaissance, our nation's culture is blossoming. We seem to have just entered a period of prolonged artistic innovation, especially in the fields of architecture and literature, and are reaping the rewards accordingly. This cultural evolution does not help us maintain peace within our borders, however, and our country is continuously stricken by foreign states seeking power and territorial gain. Perhaps it is time to unite in a decisive demonstration of our power — if for no other reason than to intimidate would-be usurpers by displaying a united front.

adv.d: While the terrain of our lands allows for swift transportation and travel along the coastline, the interior of the Italian peninsula is much harder to traverse in many places. Connecting not only interior locales, but also coast with coast, will ensure easier mercantile operations and improved maneuverability of our troops.

Italy is a desired possession for many foreign rulers. If we want to defend our country, we must expand recruitment for both our land and sea forces. Since Italy is vulnerable to invasions both from across the alpine passes and our vast coastline, we must ensure the army and navy are well-prepared to face any conqueror looking to disrupt the peace of the peninsula.

Our lands are blessed with many highly urbanized areas. This not only offers us ample opportunity to manufacture goods, but their mercantile connections also enable us to ship them to foreign markets for our profit. Clearing any obstruction to expanding these industries will guarantee their continued success.

With its close proximity to the Holy See, Italy has a long tradition of powerful and talented clergy in the service of the faith. Regardless of where our religious matters will take us, we should maintain good relations with our clergy.

Foreign interest in Italy has many times turned our lands into the battlefield of stronger countries. Sustaining our people during these times of need is a difficult task. Establishing secure locations to shelter our population during conflict will ensure their support during even the most dire wars.

The fertile, mild land of our peninsula is a popular place for people from bordering countries to seek their fortunes. While many of our cities already rely on labor from seasonal migrants, we should increase our efforts to settle these people into our lands permanently.

items.name: Mongolia

allow.t: Is not in a civil war

c.t: Modifier: Restorer of the Mongol Empire for 50 years

items.desc: The empire of … Khān, once the mightiest in the world, has all but disappeared. We are now a fragmented people, scattered and disconnected. But we are still Mongols, and we have never lost hope of capturing what we have lost. We must restore our legacy by replicating the Great Khān's conquests. The Mongol Empire will rise to conquer once more!

adv.d: Genghis Khān unified great swathes of territory under his banner. Having unified those territories again under the authority of a single Khān, all people in our empire shall swear allegiance to us.
The prowess of Mongolian horsemen is renowned across the entire world. Our enemies shake in terror at the sight of a dust cloud in the distance, fearing that it might signify our cavalry's approach!
Having unified all Mongolian territories under our banner, the stability and prosperity our people will be able to enjoy has not been seen since the times of the great Genghis Khān.

adv.n: The Life of a Steppe Warrior
adv.d: The steppe is a foreboding and unforgiving place for the unprepared. We are accustomed to living in this harsh environment, and as such our people are sturdy and have a knack for survival. We will ensure that all of our soldiers share these skills, and are thus able to more easily survive extreme situations.

As the original Mongols, we restored the Yeke Mongol Ulus, the Great Mongolian State, resurrecting the glory of Genghis Khān's great empire. Given the slightest chance, our people will emulate the exploits of the Great Khān and reclaim his legacy, reuniting the once-vast territories of the Mongol Khanate.

The system of yam posts all over our empire have facilitated communication and logistics since the times of the great Genghis Khān. After re-establishing and improving this system, our messengers can cross the massive expanse of our empire at speeds that were not even thought possible before.

Each of our soldiers typically maintains three or four horses, allowing them to change each time their mount becomes tired, and thereby travel at high speed for days without stopping. Furthermore, their extra mounts provide them with food reserves through mare's milk as well as horse meat, making our armies far less vulnerable to starvation than other, so-called civilized nations' armies. This allows us to outmaneuver our enemies with ease, covering a staggering amount of territory in shorter periods than they had believed to be possible.
The territories of the great Mongol Empire are home to many different peoples, all unified under the glory of the mighty Khān.
The Kheshig once formed the formidable bodyguard of the Great Mongol Khān. Their descendants will continue to protect the Khān of Mongolia as they ride into battle.
The extraordinary Genghis Khān amassed a huge army like never before seen. We are heirs to his glory, and therefore our army will outstrip even the greatest Mongol hordes of the past.

items.name: Mughal
items.desc: Our ruler has begun to lay the foundations for a new empire. Although inferior in numbers, our well-disciplined troops have won several decisive victories against the sultans of India. These battles for India are merely the first great victories in what will surely be a series of successful territorial expansions. With time, the empire of the Mughals will stretch across not only this region, but all the world.

adv.d: The Fatawa-i-Alamgiri is a sharia-based compilation, serving as the primary legal code regulating various aspects of life in our empire. It is one of the most comprehensive collections of Muslim laws, ethics, military strategies, economic policies, justice, and principles.

The Ibadat Khana - House of Worship - serves as a meeting place for spiritual leaders of diverse religions to engage in discussions and debates on religious teachings. It aims to foster understanding among different faiths, leading to the conclusion that all religions share a common goal.

A great empire demands equally monumental buildings. In our cosmopolitan realm, architects are already creating marvelous edifices that will awe generations to come. Our dynasty should be at the forefront of this movement, creating great architectural works such as the world has never seen.

The Zamindar are feudal rulers who govern our territories autonomously or semi-autonomously. While they are owners of the land they administrate and part of our nobility, in the end, they serve as internal vassals to the Crown itself.

Though we came to India as foreigners, we now rule as Indian Padishah, embracing local traditions while transcending divisions of caste and creed. As our realm is one of many faiths and cultures, our administration will draw talent from all communities, giving everyone — regardless of caste, religion, or culture — an equal opportunity to serve our great house and glorious realm.

items.name: North Sea
items.desc: The lands once owned by … extended over both sides of the …, from … to …. Although this territory has fragmented and reformed into different holdings over time, it has always been lying in wait, eagerly anticipating our rise and reclamation. It is time to establish this incredible empire once again, with all those lands coming together under our banner.

adv.d: Unmarried youths drafted from the poorest segments of society, the Azebs will not only function as soldiers and sailors, but also builders, sappers and armorers. Through a system of fortress garrisons, we will ensure that they always get paid.
In keeping with steppe traditions, our nobles are warriors of the frontier, and we shall be fearless in the fight to expand the Abode of Islam.
To embrace the future, we must remember what we learned from Persia and the Great Seljuks, and build a state that can unite disparate peoples and beliefs into a greater whole.
We hail from the steppes. The wind, the hardships, and the thrill of battle will always be in our blood, and we must never forget them.

Tasked with defending borders, leading raids, and expanding territories, these semi-autonomous leaders command loyal Ġuzāt warriors driven by religious fervor, plunder, and land grants, making them crucial to frontier stability and expansion. They can only be created through the … …, and they get the … … and …, while having greatly reduced payment obligations compared to a normal … but costing increased … and giving their overlord more …. A Uç Bey keeps its own …, which its … cannot convert or enforce.

With their proclivity for brigandage and wanton killing, they can always be relied upon to disturb the enemy's frontier.
Janissaries are the elite units of our armies, trained since childhood and forged through discipline.

The Janissaries are the elite corps only loyal to the Sultan himself. Their ranks are made up through the Devşirme System of child levy and go through strict military training. As such, the Janissaries are the most disciplined forces of the Empire.

By establishing unique codes of law in each of our empire's provinces, we can ensure that our rule will be viewed as equitable and just. These law books, known as Kanunname, will take into consideration the local circumstances and traditions of each of our diverse and far-flung provinces.

c.t: Is or was the country Ottomans (TUR)

adv.d: After surviving a turbulent period, and winning the struggle to dominate our neighboring Beyliks, the time has finally come for us to restore the borders of the once-great Sultanate of Rûm!

c.t: Is or was the country Ottomans (TUR)

adv.d: We are surrounded by enemies on all sides, making a strong military an absolute necessity. Fortunately, we are not weak people. From the irregular Ġuzāt and the Akıncılar raiders to the Sipâhi of the Ottomans, the world has come to fear and respect our military might. Let us build an army worthy of an empire, inspired by our glorious traditions and history, honing our might through the ages.

c.t: Is or was the country Ottomans (TUR)

adv.d: Our region is home to some of the most impressive madrasas and mosques in the entire Muslim world. With their meticulous attention to detail and abundant talent, our artisans shine with unmatched prowess.
By offering Timar land grants to Sipâhi cavalrymen, they can use this new state-sponsored wealth to supply themselves and their retinue. This allows us to field more formidable cavalry forces.

c.t: Is or was the country Ottomans (TUR)

adv.d: Our light cavalry regiments often raid and sometimes even settle in neighboring territories. Known for their courage in battle, they lived and operated as raiders on the frontier, often the first line of response against incursions from our rivals and perfectly positioned to attack and rout enemy trade routes.

Balancing local needs versus national interests is one of the most difficult aspects of government. Given the slow pace of communications, it can take a long time for the most basic directives to reach even relatively close provinces. We must encourage local governors towards more autonomy to ensure that local interests are served in a timely manner.

The Birûn, or the Exterior Service, comprises the group of administrators, military officers and religious scholars just outside the ruler's personal inner circle. Together, they make up an efficient bureaucracy inherited from Persia and the Great Seljuks, but adapted further by elements from Byzantium, making it uniquely Ottoman indeed.

c.t: Is or was the country Ottomans (TUR)

adv.d: Our caravanserais support the flow of commerce, information, and people from China to Europe across our lands. This proximity to important trade routes has unleashed a flood of affluence throughout our nation.

Interpreters, translators, and guides in one, the Dragomans are skilled officials who work to enhance our diplomatic and commercial efforts with different communities and countries. Most dragomans are of Greek ancestry, though some hail from Jewish, Armenian, or other multilingual backgrounds.

c.t: Is or was the country Ottomans (TUR)

adv.d: Persian has served as our administrative language for quite some time, a legacy stemming from our ancient roots. This has helped us transcend the social and cultural barriers that often arise in highly diverse nations like ours.

Also called capitulations, the Ahidnâme are contractual agreements with other nations, drawing upon both Muslim and secular law. Ahidnâme are most often used for guaranteeing the protection and rights of foreign merchants and clergy within our lands, ensuring that justice is upheld and trade can flow unhampered.

The Janissaries are the elite corps only loyal to the Sultan himself. Their ranks are made up through the Devşirme System of child levy and go through strict military training. As such, the Janissaries are the most disciplined forces of the Empire.
By keeping our unruly princes confined to a special part of the harem, the Kafes, we can prevent wanton rebellions and the rivalry between brothers that used to plague our regime.
A complex system of supply depots and lodgings for use by soldiers and officials, menzil waystations allow our armies to rely less on plunder, and remain well-supplied on every frontier.

Suleiman is remembered as one of the great rulers of history, a soldier, a lawmaker, and a reformer. In fact, while the West knows him as Suleiman the Magnificent, in his homeland, he is called 'The Lawgiver'. Central to his reforms was the re-examination of Ottoman dynastic law, Kanun, in order to bring it in line with Sharī'ah.

The Janissaries are the elite corps only loyal to the Sultan himself. Their ranks are made up through the Devşirme System of child levy and go through strict military training. As such, the Janissaries are the most disciplined forces of the Empire.

A system of tax farming where nobles purchase the right to collect revenue from parcels of land owned by the state. Muqāta'ah balances the distribution of wealth across the empire, and turns the nobility away from corruption, giving them a vested interest in supporting the state.
A vast, diverse, and highly organized bureaucracy staffed by the most skilled of scribes, the Mālīye aspires to be a fundamental and incorruptible institution of the state.
We will reform old and stagnant traditions, plant tulips in all gardens, and usher in a new golden age of commerce and connection.
This new school, Mühendishane-i Bahr-i Hümâyûn, will help us train shipwrights, naval officers, and sailors for both the navy and the merchant fleet.

The Janissaries are the elite corps only loyal to the Sultan himself. Their ranks are made up through the Devşirme System of child levy and go through strict military training. As such, the Janissaries are the most disciplined forces of the Empire.

Large empires are usually formed around a core territory, and otherwise surrounded by subject nations of somewhat dubious loyalty. We should take the necessary measures to keep these nations under our surveillance.
Âyan are provincial magnates of diverse backgrounds that wield significant local autonomy, but still provide a ready source of tax farming income and military forces for the state.

items.name: Persia
items.desc: … has been the seat of powerful empires since the ancient days of Cyrus the Great. Without these … kingdoms of the past, our modern world would be decades behind where we are now in terms of invention, science, and the arts. We now dwell in the dust of that greatness, dreaming of a unified … state, but perhaps not for much longer — the possibility of a resurrected … nation does not seem so intangible anymore. It is time for us to reclaim our glorious legacy, and to elevate one of our own with the title of Šâh.

c.t: Is or was the country Persia (IRA)

adv.d: The Islamization of Persia has been a lengthy process. It is not yet completely finished, but our religion has still become one of the major pillars of our national identity. Many of our ancient traditions have been combined with the teachings of Islam, and now make up our current core culture.

c.t: Is or was the country Persia (IRA)

adv.d: Before the Islamic Conquest of Persia, the region was home to the Sasanian Empire, which once ruled from Caucasia in the West to the Kirthar Range in the East. Many of its great cultural accomplishments have shaped our cultural and artistic identity.

c.t: Is or was the country Persia (IRA)

adv.d: The great plateau at the heart of our realm does not result in a weakness for us but instead turns into our strength. As the origin of great empires, our people have for countless generations crossed its great plains and the rugged mountain ranges surrounding it, like the Zagros or the Alborz. The same terrain that exhausts foreign armies is where our soldiers, our merchants, and our administrators thrive. We will use this familiarity to move across our lands and govern them with an ease that no outsider can match.

c.t: Is or was the country Persia (IRA)

adv.d: The Šāhnāme - the Book of Kings - is an epic poem, and a national treasure of the Farsi people. Describing the historical and mythical past of the empires which once occupied Greater Persia, its stories contribute to the Farsi culture in uncountable dimensions.

c.t: Is or was the country Persia (IRA)

adv.d: A system of upgrades to roads and bridges, a system of guards to protect the roads — for a small fee — and a chain of Caravanserai for rest and refreshment. All these improvements will help the merchants as they traverse the Silk Road, and also provide revenue for the state.

c.t: Is or was the country Persia (IRA)

adv.d: As a consequence of the Mongol invasion of the past, Persia is somewhat depopulated compared to the earlier empires which claimed these lands as their own. Promoting the practice of irrigation should help our people develop the agriculture needed to boost the local population and help us recover from the death toll of past conflicts.

c.t: Is or was the country Persia (IRA)

adv.d: The Mongol invasion of Persia was catastrophic for the entire region. Population centers of magnificent size were reduced to mere rubble. But it is finally time to rebuild what was once destroyed, and restore the awe-inspiring empire of Persia.

c.t: Is or was the country Persia (IRA)

adv.d: Horses play a fundamental role in our society. Many of our people are raised alongside their steeds, which is reflected in both the care our horse breeders take and the durability of our cavalry.

c.t: Is or was the country Persia (IRA)

adv.d: Persian is an ancient language with a history longer than the lifespan of many empires. Even the Muslim conquest could not diminish the core of the Persian identity, and many other states try to imitate our culture.

c.t: Is or was the country Persia (IRA)

adv.d: Persia has long been famous for its beautiful carpets and rugs. However, when the Mongols devastated the empire, much of this cultural heritage was lost. For Persia to fully recover its tumbled glory, we must regain our economic strength, and restoring this legendary ancient industry is the first step in that direction.

The Kızılbaş - the Red Heads - are a Shia military movement founded by the Ṣafawiyya. Guided by their religious convictions and deep ties to Sufism, these warriors are primed to fight for our state and to form the core of our army.
The Ṣafawiyya Order Hall is a building dedicated to the Sufi order of the Ṣafawiyya. While highly religious in nature, the building also serves as the military training grounds for the Kızılbaş.

No matter what the official faith of our state is, Persia will always be an inherently religious country. Every aspect of our life is guided by religious principles, and even the government itself acts with our core beliefs in mind when dealing with matters of morality and justice.

While the Kızılbaş are the backbone of the Persian military, the Qurchi are the royal bodyguards enlisted from their ranks. Instead of being given land, these soldiers are paid from the royal treasury.

The Ḡilmān are a military unit made up of formerly Christian slaves with Caucasian origins. The Ḡilmān undergo strict military training and are well-practiced in the usage of firearms, making them an essential part of the national army. They serve as a counterbalance to other influential branches of the military.

The Nāẓir, or overseers, are territorial administrators, and represent the eyes and ears of the Šâhanšâh. All actions of the court are supervised by the Nāẓir, and courtiers are promoted on their command. Even the Grand Vizier must work in association with the Nāẓir.

Persian art is highly in demand. Collectors from near and far travel here in droves to purchase our exquisite creations. We should offer state support for our talented artists, as this trade in aesthetic goods is extremely lucrative.

The Tofangchi are our musket corps. Although firearms have been in use for a while, their presence in our ranks is highly irregular, as many of our fighters prefer to use their traditional weapon of bow and arrow. The regiments of the Tofangchi aim to change this, as they are trained in the use of modern weaponry.

The Tupchi - artillery-men - are a specialized military unit that focuses on the usage of cannons and siege weapons. Similar to the Tofangchi, the Tupchi are an example of modern warfare exercised by the Persian Empire.

Although our lands are located mostly in the highlands of the Zagros Mountains, Persia does have coastal possessions. While past dynasties might have paid little attention to the maritime protection of the empire, our people are more aware of the sea, and our sailors are eager to defend our coasts.

The time of great religious divides has come to its end. In these turbulent times, Islam cannot afford any more in-fighting. We shall advocate for a policy of internal and external religious unity, and come to peace with what we used to consider heresy.

The Jazāyerchi are the elite musketeers of the empire. Equipped with heavy flintlock muskets with superior firepower and accuracy and exposed to constant drilling, the Jazāyerchi manage to overcome even the most one-sided odds in battle.

items.name: Russia
items.desc: Through conquest and diplomacy, Russia has managed to transform itself from a tiny settlement into a dominant power. After several expeditions in the east, the Mongol hordes have finally been subdued, and a centralized Russian state under the suzerainty of the Tsar is emerging. Influences from Western Europe are helping us modernize and reform our nation, and we are adopting a more modern style of education. Given our history of rapid growth and our modern political and cultural gifts, it seems only natural that the Russian Empire should rise and hold sway over lesser nations.

adv.d: The designs of Feodor Apraksin are robust and resilient, enabling ships to weather most storms that Mother Nature is able to conjure. The innovative construction greatly contributes to any burgeoning maritime ambitions.

The 'Toy Army' is organized into elite companies, forming the Imperial Guard which protects the interests of the monarchy. They are frequently involved in court ceremonies, parades, and other significant events, showcasing their importance beyond their military duties.

The Imperial University is dedicated to the study of philosophy, medicine, and law, and plays a significant role in Russian education and research. It is established as part of educational reforms conceived by polymath Mikhail Lomonosov, emphasizing the importance of scientific inquiry and innovation.

allow.t: We have emerged victorious from the … … without adopting the … tag

items.desc: At its height, the Sultanate of Rum was the major power in …. Sadly, it was fragmented by constant brutal invasions and vicious succession disputes, falling into obscurity. But we have the will and the power to reforge the broken pieces of … under one rule and restore our long-forgotten Sultanate!

The Janissaries are the elite corps only loyal to the Sultan himself. Their ranks are made up through the Devşirme System of child levy and go through strict military training. As such, the Janissaries are the most disciplined forces of the Empire.
By keeping our unruly princes confined to a special part of the harem, the Kafes, we can prevent wanton rebellions and the rivalry between brothers that used to plague our regime.
A complex system of supply depots and lodgings for use by soldiers and officials, menzil waystations allow our armies to rely less on plunder, and remain well-supplied on every frontier.

Suleiman is remembered as one of the great rulers of history, a soldier, a lawmaker, and a reformer. In fact, while the West knows him as Suleiman the Magnificent, in his homeland, he is called 'The Lawgiver'. Central to his reforms was the re-examination of Ottoman dynastic law, Kanun, in order to bring it in line with Sharī'ah.

A system of tax farming where nobles purchase the right to collect revenue from parcels of land owned by the state. Muqāta'ah balances the distribution of wealth across the empire, and turns the nobility away from corruption, giving them a vested interest in supporting the state.
A vast, diverse, and highly organized bureaucracy staffed by the most skilled of scribes, the Mālīye aspires to be a fundamental and incorruptible institution of the state.
We will reform old and stagnant traditions, plant tulips in all gardens, and usher in a new golden age of commerce and connection.
This new school, Mühendishane-i Bahr-i Hümâyûn, will help us train shipwrights, naval officers, and sailors for both the navy and the merchant fleet.

Large empires are usually formed around a core territory, and otherwise surrounded by subject nations of somewhat dubious loyalty. We should take the necessary measures to keep these nations under our surveillance.
Âyan are provincial magnates of diverse backgrounds that wield significant local autonomy, but still provide a ready source of tax farming income and military forces for the state.

items.name: Spain

allow.t: Every … in … must be … by a … … or one of our …!

items.desc: Since the defeat of the Visigoths by the … invasion in the 8th century, Iberia has been the seat of several independent kingdoms. Numerous would-be conquerors have since attempted to unify the region, proclaiming themselves rulers of 'Hispania,' 'Spania,' or — as it is now known — 'Spain.' But it is we who shall finally unify the Peninsula once and for all!

adv.d: The Christian kingdoms of Iberia claim continuity with the unified Visigothic monarchy that ruled Hispania from Toledo until the Muslim conquest of 711. Our chroniclers trace every king of León and Castile back through Pelayo to Reccared and the Toledan Crown, framing the Reconquista as a Restauratio — the restoration of one rightful Christian kingdom rather than the conquest of several. This Neo-Gothic ideology gives the Spanish Crown a unifying narrative that justifies a single peninsular monarchy stretching from the Pyrenees to the Strait of Gibraltar.

The chroniclers and jurists of the peninsular courts revive the Idea de Hispania — the Visigothic-Roman conception of Iberia as a single Christian community of crowns sharing one historical destiny and one legal inheritance. We will compile the genealogies, conciliar decrees, and crusading bulls that bind the peninsular monarchies into a recognizable political family, and our chanceries will adopt the formulas of Hispanic legitimacy that distinguish our kings from the merely regional dynasties beyond the Pyrenees. This shared ideological framework lets our chanceries draw on a common body of precedent to streamline our own lawmaking, while our place within this recognized Christian family of crowns means neighboring courts read our actions as those of a kindred realm rather than a threat.

The Spanish religious orders stand on the threshold of the Observancia — the movement for stricter monastic discipline — already taking root among the Franciscan and Dominican houses of Castile. We will extend Crown backing to the observant branches of every regular order, suppressing the conventual houses that have abandoned enclosure and redirecting their endowments toward the reformed Hieronymites, Augustinians, Carthusians, and Cistercians under joint Crown and inquisitorial visitation. This thoroughgoing reform of the regular clergy gives the Spanish Church a disciplined moral apparatus a generation before the rest of Catholic Europe even faces the question.

The Escuela de Salamanca — the school of theologians and jurists centered on the Universidad de Salamanca through the sixteenth century — applies Thomist scholastic methods to the unprecedented questions of empire, conquest, and global commerce. Francisco de Vitoria's lectures on the rights of the Amerindians, Domingo de Soto's monetary theory, and Luis de Molina's treatment of free will produce the first systematic European thinking on natural law, international law, and economic theory. This intellectual school gives the Spanish monarchy an ideological apparatus for its imperial project that no rival power can match for a generation.

Spain stands at the cusp of an unprecedented cultural flowering — the Siglo de Oro whose first stirrings are already visible in Antonio de Nebrija's Castilian grammar and the artistic circles of the Catholic Monarchs' court. We will channel royal patronage toward poets, dramatists, and painters through the Real Casa and the chapters of the religious orders, providing the institutional support that Cervantes, Lope de Vega, Velázquez, and Calderón will require to produce their masterworks. This sustained cultural investment turns Spain into the literary and artistic capital of the Catholic world for two centuries.

The Bourbon reform programs of Charles III and his ministers — Floridablanca, Aranda, and Campomanes — open Spain to the wider European Enlightenment in the second half of the eighteenth century. Gaspar Melchor de Jovellanos publishes his agrarian reports, the Reales Sociedades Económicas de Amigos del País spread across every provincial capital, and the universities of Salamanca, Alcalá, and Valencia introduce modern physics, chemistry, and political economy into their curricula; the Real Ordenanza de la Casa de la Moneda brings Newtonian assaying standards to every royal mint from Sevilla to Potosí; and the new Banco de San Carlos at Madrid pools merchant capital and Crown deposits to finance public projects at terms no private banker can offer. This intellectual and fiscal modernization gives the late Spanish monarchy the trained ministerial class, administrative innovation, public credit at sovereign rates, and silver-mint efficiency required to compete in the new continental order.

items.name: Īlkhānān
items.desc: Our empire once stretched across the world, endless and vibrant. Now it is a mere story, a historical footnote. This cannot stand — we are the heirs to the legacy of …, and we deserve more! We shall reform our once-glorious empire, uniting our people and retaking what was once ours. And then more...

adv.d: The Yäm, our ancient system of relay stations and messengers, once connected the furthest corners of the Mongol world. By restoring this vast network across Persia and beyond, we ensure that our orders are swift, our envoys safe, and our dominion responsive, just as it was in the golden days of the Khans.

What was once broken is now reborn. Our banners fly once more across Persia, invoking awe and fear in equal measure. As word of our rising power spreads, the world will remember what it means to be ruled by a true Īlkhān.

The blood of the Khāghān runs through our veins. Let no man forget that our rule was ordained on the steppes and sealed by conquest. Our horsemen remain unmatched, and our banners bear not just a name, but a birthright.

Our ancestors ruled with the sword, but their greatness was measured in palaces, libraries, and minarets. Let us follow their example and fund not only walls and roads, but mosques, gardens, and schools as testaments to Īlkhānān grandeur.

The days of pure steppe conquest lie behind us. We have sown ourselves into the soil of progress and reformation. From that soil, a more stable, sophisticated state shall grow. Though our hearts may still beat to the rhythm of the open fields, our future lies in lasting institutions, not fleeting raids.

items.name: Africa
items.desc: In days past, the Normans created a Christian kingdom in Africa, bridging both sides of the Mediterranean. But that fledgling nation was decimated, devoured by the enemies of Christ. Now that it is within our reach to do so, it is our duty to recover that territory and bring the glory of our Lord to them once again.

adv.d: Our administrative-military template descends from the Norman Kingdom of Africa established by Roger II of Sicily in the twelfth century, the brief Latin-Christian polity that spanned from Mahdia to Tripoli for a generation before its collapse. Our court chancellery preserves the chartered protocols, our knights' fee system inherits the Norman-Sicilian feudal arrangements adapted to North African territory, and our castle-architects build the squared-tower keeps that the Norman engineers introduced to the Maghrebi coast. This Norman-Sicilian inheritance gives our restored Kingdom of Africa a state-form template that no purely-Maghrebi successor could replicate from scratch.

The ancient Latin Church of North Africa, the bishoprics that once numbered nearly seven hundred sees from Augustine of Hippo's day and produced the great Donatist controversies and the foundational Latin theology, gets restored under our patronage as a functioning ecclesiastical infrastructure that actively converts the surrounding populations. Our archbishop of Carthage convenes the provincial synods, our missionary preachers move through the countryside in adapted Berber and Arabic vernaculars, and our cathedral-rebuilding programs at every major town anchor the steady conversion of Muslim and pagan-Berber communities to the Latin rite. This restored Latin episcopate gives our Catholic Maghreb polity an active church-growth engine that links us directly to the foundational age of Western Christianity.

Our Kingdom receives formal papal endorsement: the bull confirming our title as the rightful Christian sovereign of the Maghreb, our right to investiture by the Holy See, and the indulgences extending to all our subjects supporting the kingdom's defense. Our court receives the apostolic legate on a fixed protocol, our diplomatic letters to fellow Catholic sovereigns carry the papal seal of legitimacy, and our crown invokes the papal mandate at every formal ceremony. This papal endorsement gives our Latin-Christian polity a diplomatic-religious legitimacy that no Muslim successor can challenge from its own theological framework.

The Knights Hospitaller, the Order of Malta, and the Templar-successor orders integrate into our Kingdom's defensive structure: the heavily-fortified commandery network that anchors our coastal-and-inland defense, the standing brotherhood of warrior-monks that the maritime Catholic powers send us as continuous reinforcement, and the integrated fleet-and-fortress system that turns prize-captured Muslim ships back against the corsair states. Our grand-masters and our commanders sit on the royal council, our resident knights garrison every major fortified position, and our papal endowments fund the orders' permanent establishments. This military-religious orders integration gives our Kingdom a defensive backbone that no purely-feudal levy system could provide on its own.

Our feudal land tenure system (the chartered fiefs granted to crown-loyal nobles, the manorial estate organization with its dependent peasantry, and the chain-of-command that runs from crown through magnates to local lords) gets imposed on our North African territory in adapted form, replacing the older tribal-and-tribute arrangements that the prior Maghrebi regimes had used. Our chancellery surveys the estates and confirms each fief's bounds, our magnate-courts mediate inter-estate disputes, and our peasant tenant-class settles into the manorial routines that the agricultural calendar of the cool-season grain-and-vine economy prescribes. This feudal-administrative system gives our Kingdom a land-tenure-and-loyalty framework that the unsettled tribal landscapes around us cannot replicate.

Our mature missionary infrastructure (the Franciscan and Dominican preaching orders, the mission schools that teach Latin alongside the regional vernaculars, and the apostolic-vicariate residences that anchor mission stations along the coast and into the interior) develops the institutional depth that the prior generations of conversion-engine work has built up to. Our seminaries train native Latin-rite clergy from converted families, our endowments support the convert-protection charters that guarantee judicial standing for new Christians, and our vernacular catechisms circulate through every parish-school of our realm. This Catholic missionary infrastructure gives our Kingdom a sustained clergy-formation pipeline that consolidates the religious-cultural project of the prior centuries.

items.name: Andalusia

allow.t: Every … in … must be … by a … … or one of our …!

items.desc: Once all of Iberia was commanded by the glorious Muslim rulers of Al-'Andalus, who brought unparalleled beauty and innovation with their reign. Let us now repudiate the shameful … Reconquista, and retake the rightful lands of our ancestors.

adv.d: Our restoration of the Ḵilāfat Qurṭuba — the Caliphate of Córdoba — revives the ceremonial titulature of 'Abd ar-Raḥmān III, complete with the throne hall of the rebuilt Madīnat az-Zahrā, the gold-thread ṭirāz robes embroidered with the caliph's regnal year, and the Friday sermon proclaimed once more in the great mosque of Córdoba. We strike new dinars from West African gold in the name of the renewed caliph, send investiture banners to the Maghrebi sultans who acknowledge our suzerainty, and accept embassies from the Mamlūks of Cairo as equals rather than petitioners. This caliphal authority formalizes the ḏimma covenant over Córdoba's numerous Christian and Jewish subjects, binding the peninsula's diverse populations into a single project that no regional Maghrebi dynasty can easily contest.

The Yūsufiyya Andalusiyya — our network of royal madrasas built on the fourteenth-century Granadan model of Yūsuf I — establishes endowed teaching mosques at Córdoba, Seville, Toledo, Valencia, and Zaragoza, each provided with a library, a hospice, and a faculty drawn from across the Islamic world. Our scholars synthesize Andalusi Mālikī jurisprudence with the Ash'arī theology of Cairo and the philosophical revival of the Avicennan tradition imported from Persia. This state-funded learning produces a literate clergy and a class of trained jurists whose loyalty to the restored state is bound directly to the offices it endows.

Our long-distance commerce — the Ribā al-'Andalus, the commercial routes of the western Mediterranean — knits Genoese, Catalan, Maghrebi, and Mamlūk markets together through Andalusi merchant houses operating out of Almería, Málaga, Cádiz, and Tangier. Letters of credit drawn in our gold dinar circulate as far as Alexandria and Bruges, and Andalusi Jewish and Mozarab financiers underwrite trade ventures the older Christian banks would consider too risky to touch. This credit and commercial infrastructure lowers our cost of borrowing across the board while expanding the tax base on every kind of trade that crosses Iberian waters.

Our renewed pact of protection — the Amān Ahl aḏ-Ḏimma — extends formal safeguards to the Christian and Jewish communities of the restored state, regulating their churches and synagogues, their internal courts, and the jizya they pay in lieu of military service. Mudéjar and Mozarab guilds receive royal charters confirming their crafts, while the great Sephardic financial houses re-establish branches in Córdoba and Granada under sultanate protection. This convivencia framework integrates the productive non-Muslim populations into the fabric of the state and turns the diversity of our cities into a source of prosperity rather than rebellion.

The Armāda Andalusiyya — our combined armada — fuses the state navy at Almería and Cádiz with the chartered corsair fleets of Salé, Tetuán, and the Andalusi exile captains operating from Algiers, producing a single command capable of contesting the western Mediterranean against any peer Christian power. The fleet's amphibious doctrine combines galley-and-sail squadrons with embarked marine columns trained for rapid descents on enemy coasts and rapid re-embarkation under fire. This integrated naval force lets our armies project across the Strait of Gibraltar and along the African littoral faster than any opposing fleet can intercept.

Our modern revival — the Nahḍa Andalusiyya — opens with the recovered manuscripts of Ibn Rushd and az-Zahrāwī printed at the restored presses of Córdoba, gathers around the new Royal Academy of Granada under scholars in the lineage of Pascual de Gayangos and Reinhart Dozy, and flowers in the bilingual Arabic-Castilian literary journals of the late nineteenth century. We translate the new European scientific works into modern Arabic and recover the medieval Andalusi corpus from the Escorial, the Bodleian, and the libraries of Fez and Tunis. This intellectual renaissance restores our state's standing as a center of Mediterranean learning and sustains the prestige of our court well past the age in which other monarchies must purchase theirs anew.

items.name: Arabia
items.desc: The sands of … are the home and origin of the … people. Although divided into multiple tribes since their beginnings, their shared identity and traditions are undeniable, crossing the vast sands along with its peoples. … was unified once before, and it conquered nearly the entire world. Now it must do so again.

adv.d: Our lands are host to some of the most holy sites in our faith. This divine proximity makes our people connect deeply with their beliefs, inspiring them to further and further greatness.
There are many trade outposts along our coastline, dealing in precious goods both from our own lands and foreign shores. It is time that we claim our fair share of this wealth.

We must strengthen the authority of our administrative officials, such as the Bugyōshū magistrates and the Hōkōshū commanders. A strong bureaucracy can sometimes be the only thing that stands between us and an open civil war.

When the Kamakura Shogunate fell, we were the ones who protected the Emperor and the Imperial Court. This has afforded us a position at the forefront of all clans in Japan, as the true protector of the Empire and its courtly traditions.

Built around the ascetics of Zen buddhism, Higashiyama culture sees beauty in simplicity. It has promoted development of the formal tea ceremony, ikebana flower arrangements, theater, and art. This blossoming of culture has brought great prestige to those who practice the arts, and will reflect well upon our realm.
Shugo are important vassals for the Shogunate, administrating the lands in name of the Shōgun. Thanks to them, we can administer our lands better and more efficiently.

items.name: Aztecs
items.desc: The Aztec Empire stands as a symbol of divinity and imperial destiny. From the sacred city of …, our glorious leaders have succeeded in uniting large parts of … under one radiant Sun. Through faith, warfare, and sacrifice, our newfound empire shall reclaim its sacred purpose of ensuring that the heavens burn bright, and the gods are honored.

adv.d: Across lakes and valleys, our cities bind themselves through roads, markets, and shared purpose, strengthening our reach.
Warriors and nobles rise through valor and service, ensuring authority belongs to those who have truly earned it.

Our society is remarkably dynamic, offering commoners, also known as mācēhualtin, the path to become pīpiltin, or noble, by exceptional military service through the tlahuiztli honor dress rank system. This unique opportunity for upward mobility grants our people a distinct advantage over those in neighboring societies.

The refomation of our government, in an attempt to support the sprawl of our newly-attained urban territories, shall be united under firm oversight, creating a more orderly and dependable administration.
Pochtēcah merchants extend their routes far beyond our lands, enriching every marketplace loyal to the Mexihcah.
The fertile soils, forests, and mines of Ānāhuac yield immense riches, sustaining our growth and imperial ambitions. Properly utilizing these resources will bolster our affluence.
Once every fifty-two years, the world is renewed by flame, uniting the people in faith and cosmic balance.
Strangers have made contact with our people. Their unfamiliar ships and weapons instill awe and fear. Understanding their methods may be the key to survival.

Through devotion and ritual, we keep the sun's journey alive, easing the hearts and strengthening the spirit of our people. The preservation of equilibrium, and even the world, rests upon our shoulders.

items.name: Banten
items.desc: The … from … can boast of great prosperity, due to their unfettered access to both overland and maritime trade routes. Being a very well-situated port, … serves as a perfect place from which to expand … power and to spread our influence.

items.name: Bengal
items.desc: The people from … have a very distinct identity, forged on the banks of the mighty Ganges river. Millennia of overlapping cultures and traditions have led to the development of a particularly rich and unique … culture, one that should be the envy of the world. … people are proud of their history and shared traditions — united, we would be as a beacon for the rest of India.

items.name: Borneo
items.desc: The island of Borneo is bountiful and rich, both in natural resources and in the variety of peoples and cultures who call it home. Unifying us all under a single identity will ensure that our precious resources remain ours, and that only we will benefit from their exploitation.

items.name: Canada
items.desc: The land of … is vast and foreboding, yet incredibly bountiful and rich in resources. Although the terrain can be extremely harsh, there is great promise — and fortune — in these lands. If we were to declare ourselves as a unified Canadian nation and claim it for ourselves, there is no limit to the potential rewards we could reap!

items.name: Celtica

pot.t: Any primary, accepted or tolerated culture:

items.desc: The … peoples have a history spanning millennia. Although over the centuries they have suffered invasions from other peoples and seen their territory reduced to a shadow of their ancestral holdings, they have never fully lost their traditional beliefs, culture, or way of life. If a strong leader were to emerge and show them the way, the … could unite once more, and finally claim their rightful place of power in this world.

adv.d: Centuries of living under the shadow of conquest have taught our warriors the art of patience and resilience. We can rush headlong into danger, but we can also endure, defend, and strike only when the moment is right.
For millennia we have fished, traded, and fought along the wild Atlantic coasts. From these harsh waters, we have learned seamanship unmatched by any rival.
After long centuries of silence, the ancient spirit of the Celtic peoples stirs once more, ready to reclaim its place amongst the great civilizations of the world.

Our union is founded on the ideal of uniting the diverse peoples of the Celtic world under a shared banner. Through cooperation, we aim to preserve our heritage, promote our values, and ensure that the Celtic nations thrive together in the face of external pressures and changing times.
From crofter to chieftain, many have left our shores through hardship or hope, weaving a far-flung web of kinship that carries our language, customs, and pride to distant lands.

Our vision of a united Celtic world is more than an ideal - it is a rallying call to all who share our heritage. Together, we forge bonds that reach beyond borders, making our identity as enduring as the hills and seas we call home.
