items.name: León
items.desc: The Kingdom of León once stretched from the Atlantic coast to the gates of Toledo. With the wayward county of Castile long since gone its own way, only by reclaiming the Leonese heartland may we restore León to the dignity it deserves.

adv.d: Around 910 our court relocated from the mountain stronghold of Oviedo to the open plain of León, signaling that the Reconquista had pushed far enough south for the kingdom to govern from a proper city again. This move reorganized the royal household, the chancery, and the army around new logistics suited to plains rather than peaks, and gave the realm its enduring name: the Regnum Legionense. The relocation allows the Crown to coordinate its expanding territory with a speed that mountain-bound rivals struggle to match.

c.t: Is or was the country León (LON)

adv.d: The Order of Santiago, founded in 1170 under the patronage of the Leonese crown, raises a brotherhood of warrior-monks sworn to guard the pilgrim roads and press the Reconquista frontier. Its commanderies hold vast estates and field disciplined heavy infantry and the engineers to storm Moorish strongholds, answering to the Grand Master rather than to any quarrelsome count. This military-religious order gives the Leonese crown a standing armored fist that no secular vassal could match.

The great cañadas — the droving roads of León — carry vast flocks and herds on their seasonal march between the summer uplands of the Cantabrian sierras and the winter pastures of the plains. The crown charters and protects the transhumant routes, taxing the livestock and binding the herding towns to royal favor. This pastoral economy gives the realm a steady wealth in meat and a food surplus that the rain-poor meseta could not otherwise yield.

c.t: Is or was the country León (LON)

adv.d: In 1188 our king Alfonso IX summoned not only the bishops and great nobles, but also elected representatives of the cities, to the Cortes de León, the earliest parliamentary assembly in European history. These Cortes review royal taxation, deliberate on war and succession, and codify the privileges of the towns whose militias the crown depends on. This institutional partnership between crown and burghers makes our administration more efficient and our subjects more willing to grant the extraordinary taxes our wars require.

c.t: Is or was the country León (LON)

adv.d: Since the founding of our state, our armies have made consistent pushes to the south against the taifa kingdoms, reaching the Duero under Alfonso III, the Tagus under Alfonso VI, and Extremadura under Alfonso IX. Each new conquest is met with planned repoblación — colonist charters, exemption from manorial dues, and parish foundations — that transforms conquered land into Leonese territory faster than our rivals can manage. This proven expansion machinery turns every Reconquista conquest into a permanent integrated province rather than a temporary military possession.

The Tierra de Campos — the rolling clay plain between the Cea and the Pisuerga — is the granary of the Leonese crown, its open fields of wheat and barley feeding the cities of the north. Royal grants and the labor of the monastic granges keep the plough turning across estates that stretch to the horizon. This breadbasket gives the realm a grain surplus and a prosperity in the towns and cities that the mountain provinces around it cannot rival.

c.t: Is or was the country León (LON)

adv.d: The hereditary office of Adelantado Mayor de León — held by the Quiñones lineage from the fourteenth century — consolidates judicial, fiscal, and regional diplomatic authority across the Leonese realm into a single magistracy answerable directly to the Crown. We will channel correspondence with the great houses of León, the tax assessments of the merindades, and the appellate pleas from the corregimientos through this office, bypassing the slower channels of the central Castilian council. This concentrated regional authority gives our realm an administrative reach across the León territories that no Castile-wide office can match.

The maragatos of the Astorga hills make themselves the master carriers of the realm, their mule-trains hauling salt fish, colonial wares, and royal silver between the Cantabrian ports and the markets of the interior. Tight-knit and trusted, these arrieros run a credit-and-carriage network reaching every fair in León and Castile. This carting guild gives the realm an inland commerce and a merchant reach far beyond its modest towns.

The sheltered valleys of the Bierzo, ringed by mountains at the western edge of León, ripen the Mencía vines the Camino's monks have tended since the Middle Ages. Terraced slate slopes yield a vintage prized in the markets of the north and shipped down the pilgrim road. This viticulture gives the realm a high-value export from land too steep for the plough.

c.t: Is or was the country León (LON)

adv.d: Our royal mint operates as a permanent crown institution, contracting silver and copper supplies through long-term agreements and producing the coinage that pays our garrisons and tax collectors. The Real Casa de Moneda generates significant seigniorage income for the treasury while letting the crown control the silver content of every coin in circulation. This financial infrastructure lowers our cost of borrowing and gives the state a tool to manage liquidity that more disorganized monetary systems lack.

c.t: Is or was the country León (LON)

adv.d: The coal of the Bierzo and the deepening pits of the Laciana and the Nalón feed the forges and railways of an industrial age. Mining towns swell across the León mountains, served by the new lines cut down to the meseta and the coast. This coalfield makes the old kingdom of the Reconquista a fuel-house of the modern economy.

The infantry regiments raised from León and Asturias have always been considered among the steadiest in the Spanish army, and we now reorganize them into modern brigade structures with integrated artillery, light cavalry screens, and combined-arms training. Our Brigada Artillada de León and supporting field artillery units adopt the latest doctrines for combined infantry-artillery engagement on industrial battlefields. This modernization makes our brigades among the most capable formations in any campaign the kingdom undertakes.

items.name: Malacca
items.desc: Situated on a crucial maritime trade route, the straits of … have always maintained control of the trade flowing through, and thus control of its wealth. Perfectly positioned to benefit from this trade, and holding a land itself rich in resources and tradition, the … people have always flourished in these lands. With a unified identity, they will flourish even more.

adv.d: Long before our rise, the Orang Laut roamed the straits as masters of wind and tide. Now, by learning their ways and employing a select few, we guide traders through the narrow waters and shield our coast from pirates. Such vigilance ensures that all who sail to Malacca arrive safely.

As legend goes, the timid mouse deer sought refuge in what would later become our domain. Our beggining is humble, as little more than a fishing village clustered beneath the shade of the Melaka tree. From these roots shall grow a people that will one day shape the entire region.

From Arabia to China and the coasts of South Asia, merchants of every shore converge upon Malacca. Drawn by fair laws, secure waters, and bustling markets, they will form a great congregation that enriches our ports and carries our name across the seas.

Our envoys have secured recognition from China's most prestigious sovereigns. Tribute and goodwill flow between us, granting us prestige, protection, and a privileged place in the vast network of their trade.

The narrow Inner Strait of Malacca is the backbone of our maritime commerce. By controlling this vital strait, we channel the wealth of nations into our harbors and establish ourselves as the unrivaled gatekeepers of the east-west trade.

To manage the vast tide of merchants arriving at our ports, we appoint a Shāhbandar as the authority to oversee customs, resolve disputes, and organize the foreign quarters. This office brings order to our bustling entrepôt and will strengthen our role as the crossroads of the seas.

items.name: Mali
items.desc: The lands of the … have a proud history of wealth, cultural influence, and piety, exemplified by our forefather …. Although this resplendence has been lost to time, if we were united once again, we could restore the commercial networks and political unity that once made the … masters of trade, and elevate our people to never-before-seen echelons of power.

adv.d: The Epic of Sundiata tells of the legendary campaign of Sundiata Keita, the founder of the Malian Empire and hero of our people. His story has passed from generation to generation, and has always been a great source of inspiration to our people.
The Farari Corps are the elite of the Malian military. Commanders in their own right, they are highly respected for their experience and bravery.
The Kouroukan Fouga is the basic constitution of Mali. It covers every aspect of living, from simple family life in the villages all the way to the sovereignty of the Mansa.

The Mandekalu Levies are the backbone of the Malian military. Freemen of the Empire are called to arms in times of war, and it is a great honor for them to participate in these battles with their own weapons.

Originally, all soldiers in the Kèlè-Bolo levies are horon, or 'freemen', but the latest developments in Mali have forced the inclusion of jonow, 'slaves', to serve in the army as fighters instead of weapon-bearers. These slave warriors would thereafter be known as 'Sofa', protecting fortifications as part of garrison forces.

The Kèlè-Koun, or 'war-head', are the commanders of infantry fighting for Empire, called the Kèlè-Bolo, or 'war-arm'. Unlike the Ton-Tigi, the feudal lords of Mali, the Kèlè-Koun are not necessarily part of the Nobility. The Kèlè-Koun have jonow, 'slaves', serving as carriers of the weapons and equipment until their inclusion in the Sofa battalions.

The twin gold fields at Bambuk and Bure are renowned as the largest gold deposits anyone has ever heard of, and they belong to us! Bure's gold mines in particular produced fantastic wealth that famously destabilized the entire Egyptian economy through inflation when Mansa Mūsā visited there. Our economy, though, is used to a constant influx of gold, and is more difficult to inflate.

The Sahara is not static. It can wax and wane depending on rainfall, and the habitable belt known as the Sahel, where we reside, can grow or shrink accordingly. A major drought could render much of our kingdom useless desert, an addition to the Sahara where no one reigns but death. However, in good years, we might reclaim some of the marginal lands from the Sahara and make it productive again.

According to the legendary Mansa Mūsā, his predecessor started a journey across the Atlantic Ocean in hopes of discovering the furthest limits of the ocean. While some among the ruling class consider this endeavor a shameful abdication of duty, others see this as inspiration to explore corners of the world previously unknown to man.

Whether pagan or Muslim, Mandinka men have been the greatest fighters the Sahel has ever seen. The courage of our troops is admirable, as is their pride. When the Mansa raises an army, not only is it the largest in all the Sahel, it is the best!

In our kingdom, Salt is worth its cost in gold. But south of us, in the great forests of the Ashanti and the Yoruba, salt is worth considerably more than gold. Luckily for us, we have our own supply of Salt, and enough gold to obtain as much as we could ever want. Perhaps we could find yet more markets of people for whom Salt is more valuable than gold?

Even before our Empire existed, the great Wagadou, the Ghana Empire that preceded us, sold Slaves across the desert to the Arabs. We have followed suit all these years, supplying the Arab world with a vast number of Slaves. Now the Europeans clamor for even more Slaves to work their holdings in the so-called New World. We have had little report, but the amount of Slaves they demand is truly stunning, and they keep coming back, sometimes even raiding our shores and abducting our subjects. The time has come to impose order on this trade and restrict the Europeans to select commercial ports where they will purchase, not steal, Slaves.

items.name: Mallorca
items.desc: The short-lived Kingdom of Majorca, born of the testamentary division of the Aragonese crown, mastered the trade routes of the western Mediterranean from its court at Palma. By restoring the kingdom and its Balearic heart, we shall once again grow rich from the bounty of the sea.

adv.d: The Carta de Franquesa granted by King Jaume I in 1230 — in the very year following the conquest of Mayūrqa — establishes the bedrock of Mallorcan liberty: the freedom of the new settlers from servile dues, the right of the universitat to elect its own jurats, and the exemption of our merchants from the harshest royal levies. Each of the foranes — the rural communities scattered across the island — receives these privileges alongside Palma's burghers, binding the entire repopulation under a single charter rather than a feudal patchwork. This founding-charter framework gives every Mallorcan household a direct stake in defending royal authority and softens the diplomatic friction we encounter when our envoys speak abroad of a kingdom under law.

Our Escola Cartogràfica Mallorquina gathers Jewish and Christian map-makers around the Cresques family of Palma — Abraham and his son Jafudà — who produces dozens of working portolan charts for the courts of Aragon, France, and Castile. Their workshops standardize the conventions of compass roses, rhumb lines, and named ports that every Mediterranean and Atlantic captain will rely on for two centuries. This concentration of cartographic learning raises the prestige of our Crown across Christendom and seeds a printing tradition in our presses that nourishes scholarship well beyond cartography alone.

Royal patents de cors authorize our captains to arm fast galleys and brigantines at private expense for raids against Barbary and Genoese shipping, as well as any other commerce hostile to the Crown. The corsair fraternity at Palma maintains its own rolls of veteran helmsmen, gunners, and boatswains that the royal navy draws upon in time of war, blurring the line between privateer and naval reservist into a single pool of seafaring manpower. This deep reservoir of trained crews fills our fleets faster than any state-recruited navy can and lets our squadrons reach distant station before any peer Mediterranean force has cleared harbor.

A network of torres costaneres — squat circular watchtowers of marès stone — rings Mallorca, Menorca, Ibiza, and Formentera. The towers are within sight of one another, manned by parish levies who light signal fires the instant a Barbary sail appears on the horizon. Each tower is paired with a fortified parish church and a refuge cistern, so that no coastal community is more than an hour from defensible walls and stored water. This island-wide defensive lattice raises the cost of any amphibious assault on our shores and lets a smaller garrison defend a longer perimeter than the establishment of any peer realm could match.

The pale marès limestone of Mallorca and the dark slate of Menorca feed an organized indústria lapidària that supplies Iberian construction sites from Palma's cathedrals and Catalan coastal forts to American colonial churches. Our quarrymen in Santanyí and Felanitx work seasonally under contract to royal arsenals, paying tribute in cut blocks rather than coin and earning a reputation for the precision of their dressed ashlar. This organized stone-cutting industry raises the productive efficiency of every Mallorcan workshop and accelerates every royal building project across our realm.

The literary flowering of our islands through the Escola Mallorquina restores Mallorcan letters to the European mainstream after generations in which our tongue survived only in private devotion and folk song. We will sponsor the Pollença and Palma poetic circles whose clear, classicizing Catalan draws on both the Greco-Latin canon and the rugged landscape of the Serra de Tramuntana, channeling their journals and verses through every shipping route between the islands and the mainland. This literary revival deepens the islanders' identification with their own language and softens the assimilation of mainland migrants, who absorb the local idiom through the school's widely-read pages.

items.name: Maya
items.desc: For centuries, our people have been divided into independent cities, which themselves have been locked in bitter competition with each other. This has created an environment of energy and innovation, but we lack the unity needed to stay strong in the face of external pressures. By unifying all Mayan settlements into a single realm, our nation will thrive, and reach the heights of power it soundly deserves to reach.

items.name: Morocco
items.desc: The history of our nation is one of rise and fall, great dynasties collapsing only to be reborn. Yet among the ebb and flow of this dynastic chaos, our culture shines like a precious jewel. We are a people of art, learning, science, and progress, the light in this region. Our nation must achieve lasting stability and grow powerful through unity, ensuring the prosperity of our people and striking fear into the hearts of our enemies.

adv.d: The fleet of the al-Muwaḥḥidūn caliphs at Marrakesh, sustained by tribute-payments from the Italian maritime republics under Ya'qūb al-Manṣūr and command-coordinated from the imperial capital, established Moroccan naval supremacy in the western Mediterranean for two centuries. Our sultans inherit not only the docks at Salé, Asilah, and Larache but the doctrine of strategic centralization: fleets dispatched against single objectives at the order of Marrakesh, rather than the dispersed privateering that any coastal corsair captain could mount on his own. This imperial command tradition lets our navy operate as a coherent strategic instrument that fragmented coastal corsair fleets cannot match.

The Banū Marīn, Zenata Berbers from the eastern plateaus, supplant the failing Almohads at Marrakesh and rebuild the imperial state around a reformed makhzen chancery at Fez al-Jadid, a streamlined dīwān of provincial governors, and a court ceremonial purged of Almohad religious-doctrinal overreach. The dynastic transition consolidates a leaner, administratively coherent imperial throne than the sprawling caliphate it replaces. This Marinid reorganization gives our court a functional centralized apparatus that the Almohad inheritance alone could not have provided.

The mountain ranges that crown our territory (the High Atlas, the Middle Atlas, the Anti-Atlas, and the Rif) are the reason no foreign empire has ever held Morocco in lasting submission. Our Amazigh mountain clans have garrisoned the passes since the Roman attempts of Pliny's day, and our network of qaṣbah fortresses at Telouet, Aït Benhaddou, and the high valleys lets us hold defensible ground against any invader. This fortified geography makes Morocco the only maghreb_region_ADJ kingdom whose interior cannot be conquered by sea or by Saharan crossing.

Marinid sultans endow a network of imperial madrasas across Fez and the surrounding cities (the Bū 'Ināniyya, the 'Aṭṭārīn, the Bū 'Ināniyya of Meknes, the Ṣahrīj, and the Miṣbāḥiyya), each with mosque, library, hospice, teaching staff, and student stipends paid from the sultanic treasury. The graduates staff the qāḍī benches, the chancery scribes, and the sermon-givers of the kingdom, binding the religious establishment to the imperial throne through shared training. This sultan-funded scholarship raises the literate ceiling of our state and draws reformist scholars from across the Muslim world to our court.

Our imperial throne rests on a dual capital axis: Marrakesh holds the ceremonial prestige inherited from Almohad caliphal claims, while Fez al-Jadid serves as the administrative-religious heart of the realm. Each capital governs its own half of our territory through its own dīwāns and military command, while the sultan circulates between them on a yearly ceremonial circuit asserting central authority across the kingdom. This dual-capital arrangement projects our reach further across our territory than any single-seat Maghrebi state can hope to match.

Our sugar plantations and refining mills at Chichaoua, the Sus valley, and the Tadla plain transform Moroccan agriculture into a vertically-integrated industrial-export complex: sultanic charters grant tax-exempt status to the cane plantations, royal mills process the cane into refined loaves, and the imperial treasury takes a share at every stage. Our sukkar al-Maghribī reaches European bookkeepers, druggists, and confectioners through the Atlantic ports, commanding premium prices over Madeiran and Brazilian competitors. This vertically-integrated sugar industry generates revenue our central treasury draws upon directly and gives the Moroccan crown a luxury-export advantage no other Maghrebi state can match.

The Banū Sa'd, descended from the Prophet Muḥammad through Ḥasan ibn 'Alī and long settled in the Drâa Valley as a family of sharifian local notables, emerge in the early sixteenth century as claimants to the sultanate against the failing Waṭṭāsids. Their dynastic mission, to restore unified Moroccan-Arab imperial authority under a sharifian crown, wins them swift support from the ulema of Fez and Marrakesh, the trans-Saharan caravan masters, and the urban Andalusi exile communities. This dynastic emergence lets our envoys claim the prestige of prophetic descent across the courts of the Muslim Mediterranean and the Saharan trade world.

Our court under great sultans of the imperial heyday, the era subsequent generations remember as the dhahabī or golden age, accumulates wealth on a scale no later Maghrebi state can equal. Gold flows in from the Saharan termini at Sijilmasa, Walata, and Timbuktu; refined sugar departs the Atlantic ports for European confectioners; ambassadors arrive from courts across Christendom and the Sublime Porte seeking alliance or commerce. This sustained prosperity gives our state a fiscal cushion that subsequent reigns draw upon to fund military campaigns, religious endowments, and dynastic ceremonies that lesser states cannot afford.

Morocco's strategic position controlling the western Mediterranean gateway and the Atlantic re-supply route makes us the indispensable diplomatic counterweight for any European power seeking advantage against another. Our envoys at foreign courts negotiate as equals; the Sublime Door of Marrakesh receives ambassadors, signs commerce treaties, and arbitrates disputes between Christian princes who would never accept such mediation from any other Muslim sovereign. This unique diplomatic standing gives the Moroccan throne leverage in European affairs that no other Maghrebi or sub-Saharan state can match.

The Black Guard is an elite corps of slave soldiers: enslaved men, haratin, and free Muslims raised from childhood to a strict religious creed and drilled in archery, horsemanship, and musketry. They form the backbone of our army.

Our sultans have granted military estates to the jaysh tribes, chiefly the Banū Ma'qil and Banū Ḥassān, in exchange for permanent cavalry service to the throne. These warrior clans hold their lands tax-free and answer the sultan's call with their full mounted strength, providing the mobile striking force that the makhzen deploys against rebellious cities and Sahel raids. This integration of pastoral Arab tribes into a feudal military system gives Morocco a standing cavalry reserve at no fiscal cost to the central treasury.

The constitutional doctrine of sharifian inviolability holds that our sultan, descended from the Prophet through Ḥasan ibn 'Alī, cannot be challenged on the same footing as a mere governor or qā'id. Provincial revolts may topple individual ummāl, urban risings may unseat hated tax-collectors, and tribal confederations may resist particular royal commands, but the sharifian crown itself remains constitutionally sacrosanct in the eyes of the ulema and the bay'a-bound notables. This deep dynastic legitimacy lets our state weather provincial unrest that would topple monarchies dependent on purely secular authority.

Successive nineteenth-century sultans pursue a continuous program of administrative, fiscal, and military modernization: recruiting foreign technical advisors, restructuring the makhzen chancery, modernizing the imperial arsenals, and standardizing tax collection across the realm. Each reform faces resistance from entrenched tribal and ulema interests, but a slow institutional pattern of reform-and-adjustment gradually emerges and persists across changing sultans. This sustained adaptation lets our crown promote technicians, engineers, and modern administrators into positions of state authority while raising the efficiency of every fiscal flow into the treasury.

The traditional patchwork of kharāj, 'ushūr, zakāt, and city-guild gharāma taxes is repeatedly reorganized into more efficient consolidated forms: the unified per-capita tertib on the rural plain, the standardized urban tax, and the regularized Atlantic-port customs assessments. Our merchants gain predictability in their fiscal burdens, our Jewish-Andalusi banking houses at Tetouan and Mogador refine their lending terms accordingly, and our treasury captures revenue that previously leaked through the cracks of overlapping exemptions. This continuous fiscal modernization gives our crown the financial leverage to fund modern armies and infrastructure that purely traditional tax regimes cannot sustain.

items.name: Navarre
items.desc: Originally a march of the Carolingian Empire, the legendary … kingdom founded by the warlord Íñigo Arista has been lost for too long. These lands must be reunited, and the … peoples unified under the chained banner of Navarre!

c.t: Is or was the country Navarre (NAV)

adv.d: The shipwrights of Pasaia, Mutriku, and Lekeitio have built whaling ketches, herring busses, and trans-Atlantic cargo carriers for foreign clients since the thirteenth century. The Navarrese Crown charters our arsenals to standardize hull designs based on local oak, Pyrenean iron fittings, and modular construction methods that allow rapid replacement of damaged vessels. This concentrated shipbuilding capacity makes Navarre the only Iberian Crown able to launch fully equipped war squadrons within a single season of warning.

c.t: Is or was the country Navarre (NAV)

adv.d: At the Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa in 1212, Sancho VII the Strong of Navarre broke the Almohad center personally with the chivalry of Navarre, taking the Caliph's golden tent chains that now adorn the royal arms of Navarre. Though landlocked by the later rise of Castile and Aragon, every generation of Navarrese knights is raised on the legend of Sancho's charge and committed to fight in every major Christian campaign on the peninsula. This Crusader heritage gives the Navarrese Crown a sacral standing on the Iberian Peninsula that its small size could otherwise never command.

u: Chivalric order: Order of the White Greyhound

c.t: Is or was the country Navarre (NAV)

adv.d: Straddling the Pyrenees, Navarre receives Renaissance humanism through two channels — the universities of Bordeaux and Paris from the north, and Salamanca and Alcalá from the south. The court of John III d'Albret and Catherine of Foix corresponds with Erasmus, hosts the philosophical lectures of Pedro de Atarrabia, and supports the first Basque-language publication, Bernart Etxepare's Linguae Vasconum Primitiae. This intellectual openness produces a small but cosmopolitan elite uniquely suited to mediating between French and Castilian humanism.

c.t: Is or was the country Navarre (NAV)

adv.d: Sandwiched between Castile, Aragon, the Crown of England in Gascony, and a hungry France beyond the passes, Navarre has never enjoyed the luxury of unprepared peace. The Pyrenean Cortes de Navarra maintains a permanent inventory of stored grain, beacon towers along every pass, and a rotating militia summoned by village criers from one valley to the next. This perpetual readiness allows a kingdom of two hundred thousand souls to mobilize within forty-eight hours of any incursion across its mountain frontiers.

c.t: Is or was the country Navarre (NAV)

adv.d: At the Battle of Roncesvalles in 778, a Basque ambush annihilated the Frankish rearguard of Charlemagne and killed Count Roland of Brittany, a feat that has lived in European memory through the Chanson de Roland. The Catalan Company under Roger de Flor, recruited largely from Navarrese and Aragonese mountaineers, carved a path of terror through the Byzantine Empire in 1303 and held the Duchy of Athens for three generations. This reputation for ferocity precedes our infantry into every theater, granting Navarrese commanders a psychological advantage before the first volley is fired.

c.t: Is or was the country Navarre (NAV)

adv.d: The Foruak — known as Fueros in Castilian usage and corresponding to the body of customary laws governing each Basque province — guarantee local self-government in exchange for loyalty to the Navarrese Crown. Each historical territory elects a Diputación Foral responsible to its general assembly, the Junta General, while remaining within the wider royal administration. This intermediate level of government gives the Crown efficient access to taxes and soldiers without provoking the violent fueros-defending revolts that have wrecked rival Iberian centralization projects.

c.t: Is or was the country Navarre (NAV)

adv.d: Navarrese merchants have built commercial networks along the Pyrenean wool routes between Castile, Aragon, and the French Atlantic ports since the early Middle Ages. Through the consulates of Bayonne and Tudela, our trading houses now handle the export of Castilian merino to Flanders, the import of English cloth to inland Iberia, and the silver-and-spice exchanges of the Bordeaux fair. This commercial network gives a landlocked kingdom of mountains a stake in every major continental trade artery from the Channel to Granada.

c.t: Is or was the country Navarre (NAV)

adv.d: With Spain consolidating to the south and France pressing its absolutist ambitions to the north, Navarre cannot rely on improvised levies and Pyrenean valleys alone for its defense. We will establish the Tercio de Navarra, a permanent regiment quartered at Pamplona and recruited from each of the kingdom's six merindades according to fixed quotas. This standing professional infantry doubles our peacetime military strength and provides the trained cadre around which a wartime army of conscripts can be rapidly built.

c.t: Is or was the country Navarre (NAV)

adv.d: The mercantile houses of Pamplona, Tudela, and Bilbao have built fortunes on the Castilian wool trade, the Atlantic cod trade, and the long-distance commerce in iron and arms supplied to every major European power. We extend their reach through the Royal Trade Privileges, granting Navarrese merchants reduced customs in every Spanish American port and consular protection in the Hanseatic cities. This international commercial network channels a disproportionate share of Atlantic and Mediterranean trade returns through our small kingdom's treasury.

c.t: Is or was the country Navarre (NAV)

adv.d: To replace the apprenticeship-based officer corps of the old Tercio de Navarra, the Crown has founded the Royal Military Academy of Pamplona under the direction of veterans of the Italian campaigns. The curriculum combines fortification engineering on the Vauban model, modern artillery science, and the tactical theory of the new linear infantry formations. This professional officer school standardizes military doctrine across the Navarrese army and produces a generation of trained commanders for the king's broader Iberian forces.

c.t: Is or was the country Navarre (NAV)

adv.d: The Cámara de Comptos Reales of Pamplona, founded as the first permanent royal exchequer on the Peninsula, has produced the longest continuous fiscal archive in Iberia. We modernize its procedures with Enlightenment-era double-entry bookkeeping, a numbered file system inspired by French royal practice, and the appointment of trained jurists from the University of Oñati to the senior accountancies. This bureaucratic apparatus extracts revenue from the kingdom with a precision that older Iberian crowns cannot match.

c.t: Is or was the country Navarre (NAV)

adv.d: The introduction of the rifled musket and the percussion cap requires a new tactical doctrine of skirmishing in dispersed open order — a fighting style for which the Pyrenean terrain has trained the Navarrese infantry for generations. The Royal Academy of Pamplona is developing the Marcha de Cazadores, a fast-pace marching cadence and dispersion drill that lets entire battalions advance under cover while maintaining unit cohesion. This drill makes Navarrese light infantry the model for every Iberian army adapting to the realities of rifled-weapon warfare.

items.name: Nepal
items.desc: Despite their proud and ancient histories, the Himalayan kingdoms remain fragmented and weak. By uniting the entire region under one ruler, we could become an unstoppable force, capable of challenging the soft, voluptuous rulers of Hindustan. Content to live off their wealth, they have squandered their riches for generations, and will be no match for our hardened armies.

c.t: Is or was the country Nepal (NPL)

adv.d: Our people have lived since time immemorial in the shadow of very mountains that sustain the Heavens. The high passes, the steep ridgelines, the deep-cut river valleys — these are not obstacles to us but the very fabric of our homeland. Even the air itself is different than that of the lowlands, and no army from the plains can expect to move through these lands as our soldiers do.

c.t: Is or was the country Nepal (NPL)

adv.d: Gurkha are troops of Nepali origins (as their name are quite interchangeable) who are infamous for their unbreakable bravery and discipline in combat.

c.t: Is or was the country Nepal (NPL)

adv.d: The Divya Upadesh lays out nine principles that form the core of political and national life in Nepal, as well as guidelines for successful foreign policy. It encapsulates centuries of Nepali thought on governance, war, and peace. Following these principles, Nepal shall be able to avoid the subversion of nearby empires and marauding foreigners.

items.name: Netherlands
items.desc: The Dutch are emerging as one of Europe's most capable naval and colonial powers. Lucrative trade opportunities, locally and overseas, have resulted in a swift evolution that has transformed the country into one of the first capitalist nations in history. Complementing this superlative economic acumen are the Dutch talents for innovation and creativity, which turn our culture into a light shining all over the world. A unified Dutch state, therefore, stands to be one of the wealthiest and most influential of all time.

adv.d: While our people always enjoyed superior literacy rates at all levels of society, this advantage is becoming more apparent in the world taking shape before us. Only those with a limited understanding would not take advantage of and increase this edge.

Standard volley fire involved each rank delivering its volley in one go to maximize firepower. But we have developed a different system of firing by platoon, with the idea being that one part of the regiment would always be firing at the enemy while others reloaded and got ready for the next volley. This removed time between attacks that the enemy could use to recover or otherwise gain an advantage.

Our nation is blessed with a well-established hub of cities focused on trade, and adventurous sailors willing to bring riches from all over the world back home. These seafarers will be an excellent way for us to trade with other nations and make significant profits.

the Netherlands has historically been at the forefront of technological and cultural advancements. We must continue to patronize inventors, artists, and writers to maintain our edge over other nations.

Our borders are not well-defended by natural features, as is the case in some other nations. However, we have wit and wisdom in abundance, enough to construct the mightiest fortifications possible to deter our enemies and protect our families.

For too long, our nation has been unevenly governed by multiple Stadtholders across different provinces, with the most powerful acting as Primus inter Pares among their peers. It is time to make the position hereditary and concentrate authority in a single ruler.

items.name: Nu Tireni
items.desc: The … people of … have always divided themselves into separate tribes, deeply connected through kinship and marriage. On one hand, our separation and individualism has created a cultural resilience that gives our traditional ways room to thrive. On the other hand, we could more easily repel attempted invaders were we to unite under a single banner and present our people as a holistic power. Perhaps this is the way of our future?

items.name: Nubia
items.desc: Our nation is ancient, but it has not endured. Divided among competing rulers, we have one by one fallen prey to stronger enemies. The lands before the Nile Cataracts must be unified under a single rule, capable of resisting those enemies and defeating them in battle, if we are ever to rise again as a realized power in this world.

items.name: Old North
items.desc: The … peoples could once be found all over the region of …. Although they were first forced away from the southern lands by both the Romans and the Anglo-Saxons, they managed to maintain a strong presence in the northern parts of the island until the arrival of the … peoples. Over time, we started losing our mother tongue and culture... but no more! It is time to reclaim the old kingdom of the north, and see the … people unified by law as well as by language.

items.name: Poland
items.desc: The kingdom that the Piasts once worked so hard to reunify is now divided and without leadership. There is too much glory in our history and too much promise in our future to allow Poland to remain cut into pieces — we must strive to unite the Polish people and create a nation that will shine even brighter than our kingdoms of the past!

adv.d: Castellans represent the voice of the monarch across our domain. They are in charge of gathering taxes and enforcing the rule of law, and may even execute justice in the name of the Crown.
The fertile lands of our domain are a coveted destination for many migrants, primarily those of lower status, seeking a better and more prosperous life.

Known as the General Charter of Jewish Liberties, this legislation contains articles that allow all Jews in our realm the freedom to worship, trade, and travel. The statute also attempts to reduce the number of blood libel accusations against Jews propagated by the Catholic Church.

This legislation establishes the kingdom as an indivisible, collective entity, owned not by any single dynasty or monarch but by the entire noble class. Rulers serve the realm, they do not own it. This concept of collectivity is deeply entrenched in our society.

The Folwark System was a system of production that emphasized creating agricultural surpluses. Peasants were encouraged to work through either the use of rents or through compulsion. This system formed the bedrock of our economy.

In an attempt to reform our monetary system, we will introduce a new currency, the Kraków Grosz. Minted from silver, these coins are destined to challenge the power of the Bohemian Prague Groschen and help establish our realm as pioneers of centralized taxation.

For centuries, we have used wood to build our towns and defenses, but we will now systematically upgrade our infrastructure by replacing more vulnerable wooden structures with stronger ones. We have inherited wooden towns, but we shall leave them fortified with stone and brick.

b: Allows Council of Three Lands: yes
adv.d: Our country has a long-standing history of accepting destitute, persecuted Jewish people. To that end, a council that will look after their needs and advocate for their rights will benefit the stability and spiritual strength of this realm.

Inspired by the ideals of the Italian Renaissance, we are experiencing a cultural golden age. Our literary achievements, architectural splendors, and cultivated atmosphere of religious tolerance have all led to a blossoming of culture across our land.

The fertile fields of our domain are home to Europe's richest grain crops, in part thanks to the Folwark System. Through our grace, we supply the markets beyond our borders, ensuring our people continue to prosper and never go hungry.

The hussars were originally light cavalry troops used for scouting, but with the decline of the old feudal army, we have switched over to professional regiments, the core of which shall be made up of these heavier, armored hussars. The fear of these winged warriors shall make our enemies tremble in the night like children!

The evolution of Polish hussars entailed the adoption of heavier armor with red and white colors. They used a longer lance of around six meters, which made their charge incredibly devastating, often breaking the morale of their foes and causing them to rout.
The 'Compute Army' was based around an annual budget calculated and approved by the Sejm. The idea behind this was to provide the Commonwealth with a stable standing army for defense.

If we are to survive and continue to prosper, our governmental mechanism must run efficiently and be based on robust foundations. The parliament shall adopt modernized procedures and strengthen its authority. The goals of this evolution are to curtail the power of the nobility and mitigate the escalating abuses of serfdom.

Our government's need for capable administrators has led to systematic education reform. We will establish the first education ministry in Europe, devoted to spreading literacy throughout our population, which will hopefully lead to an increase in qualified candidates to staff our expanding administration.
By establishing the 'Knight's School' to train noble youth in military science and their patriotic duty, we will forge generations of capable, dedicated military and civil personnel.

items.name: Pomerania
items.desc: Pomeranian territory occupies a vital position along the Baltic coastline. If we want to profit from our strategic position, and take advantage of being on a busy trade route, we must do away with the old divisions and succession squabbles, and reform a united Pomeranian Duchy.

items.name: Portugal
items.desc: Wrested from the Kingdom of León in the twelfth century, Portugal has hewed to its own destiny ever since. With our northern lands reunited under our crown, we may yet turn our gaze southward against the Muslim taifas and seaward to lands beyond the horizon.

c.t: Is or was the country Portugal (POR)

adv.d: The white monks of Cister — at Alcobaça, Bouro, and Tarouca — drain the marshes, clear the scrub, and plant the granges of the Estremadura and the Alentejo in the wake of the Reconquista. Their lay brothers and the settlers drawn by monastic forais turn empty borderland into wheat-fields, vineyards, and orchards. This Cistercian husbandry feeds the young kingdom and fixes a Christian peasantry on land barely wrested from the Moor.

At the Battle of Ourique in 1139, Count Afonso Henriques defeated a numerically superior Almoravid force in the contested borderlands of the Alentejo. The victory was sanctified by his troops' acclamation as king on the field, the rumored vision of Christ before the battle, and the eventual Manifestis Probatum of 1179 in which Pope Alexander III recognized Portugal as a kingdom. This founding triumph anchors Portuguese royal legitimacy in divine endorsement and battlefield achievement rather than dynastic descent, distinguishing our kingship from the rest of Iberia.

c.t: Is or was the country Portugal (POR)

adv.d: Lisbon, at the broad mouth of the Tejo, grows into the great entrepôt of the western seaboard, where the salt, wine, and cork of the interior meet the cloth and metals of the north. Genoese and Flemish factors house themselves along the riverfront, and the crown's customs swell with the traffic of two seas. This Tagus emporium makes the capital the commercial heart of the realm well before the first caravel rounds Bojador.

Under Prince Henry the Navigator, the maritime school at Sagres gathers Genoese pilots, Catalan cartographers, and Portuguese shipwrights to systematize the navigation of the African Atlantic. Gil Eanes rounds Cape Bojador, the caravels reach Sierra Leone, and Bartolomeu Dias clears the Cape of Good Hope, each voyage extending our charts a hundred leagues further south. This sustained royal investment in exploration positions Portugal as the only kingdom in Europe with the institutional patience to wait two generations for an oceanic payoff.

c.t: Is or was the country Portugal (POR)

adv.d: The Carreira da Índia — the annual round voyage from Lisbon to Goa and back around the Cape — becomes the longest regular sea route in the world, its great naus beating south on the volta do mar and home laden with pepper and cinnamon. Our pilots master the monsoon timetable and the deep-ocean navigation the run demands. This India run gives the realm a maritime reach and a spice revenue out of all proportion to its size.

The Feitorias — fortified trading factories established along the African and Asian littorals from the late fifteenth century — combine warehouse, garrison, customs house, and chapel under a single royal Feitor. Beginning with São Jorge da Mina and extending to Sofala, Hormuz, Goa, Malacca, and Macau, the network monopolizes choke-points along the spice routes without requiring large inland conquests. This factory-trading model gives Portugal control over global commerce on an unmatched ratio of trade volume to occupying troops, sustained by maritime supremacy alone.

The Crown claims a monopólio over the pepper, cinnamon, and clove passing through … ports, licensing which merchants may carry them and levying its fifth on every cargo that lands. By binding the spice trade to royal charter rather than to whichever captain returns first, the treasury turns the gamble of the sea into a steady and predictable source of revenue.

c.t: Is or was the country Portugal (POR)

adv.d: The Ordenanças reform of King Sebastian organizes every Portuguese township into companies of armed citizens led by elected Capitães-mores, drilled monthly and obliged to muster for any royal proclamation of arms. The Filipine reforms standardize equipment, fortify the muster rolls, and require every male between sixteen and sixty to enroll in his parish company. This universal militia system gives the kingdom a permanent reserve of trained manpower that can be mobilized for colonial campaigns or domestic defense without the cost of a standing army.

The realm casts off the long union with Castile and acclaims a native dynasty, opening a generation of war along the Alentejo frontier. New bulwarked fortresses rise, fresh regiments are raised from every parish, and the alliances that guarantee its sovereignty are sealed. This restoration of independence rallies the whole nation behind the legitimate crown as no foreign or formed claimant ever could.

c.t: Is or was the country Portugal (POR)

adv.d: After two centuries of contested compromise with the noble Cortes of Évora, Lisbon, and Coimbra, the Crown moves to consolidate executive authority on the model of the French and Spanish monarchies. King Joseph I and his chief minister the Marquis of Pombal abolish the surviving feudal privileges, expropriate the Jesuit estates, and reform the royal council into a streamlined cabinet of professional ministers. This concentration of authority lets the Crown drive reform programs through with the speed required by the new commercial economy, free of the obstructionism that aristocratic assemblies had previously imposed.

c.t: Is or was the country Portugal (POR)

adv.d: The crown overhauls its government with professional secretariats of state, a reformed treasury, and a streamlined cabinet of salaried ministers answerable directly to the king. Old feudal jurisdictions give way to appointed magistrates, and the overseas revenues are routed through a single council. This administrative modernization lets the crown drive reform with a speed the old conciliar tangle could never allow.

c.t: Is or was the country Portugal (POR)

adv.d: Nicknamed the Fighting Cocks, the Caçadores are an elite light infantry unit in the Portuguese Army who wear brown uniforms to distinguish them from regular soldiers.

adv.n: Royal Academy of Fortification, Artillery, and Drawing
adv.d: Queen Maria I establishes the Academia Real de Fortificação, Artilharia e Desenho at the Castle of São Jorge in Lisbon, succeeding the seventeenth-century military classes of Luís Serrão Pimentel. The curriculum unites Vauban-style fortification, Frézier descriptive geometry, and the modern artillery doctrines tested by French and Prussian engineers, taught by Manuel de Sousa Ramos and the royal engineer corps. This unified military academy gives the Portuguese army an officer corps trained to a continental European standard, preserving the kingdom's technical credibility through the wars of the coming century.

items.name: Prussia

c.t: Member of organization: Holy Roman Empire

items.desc: The land once conquered and Germanized by the Teutonic Order will always require protection against rapacious outside forces. But should the Order fail in this duty, we can take their place and usher in a new era of prosperity and Prussian discipline.

adv.d: Governing two territories separated by foreign lands demands more than ordinary administration. We will ensure our laws reach the far corners of our realm and that every magistrate answers to the same authority, however distant from the capital he may be.

The knights who carved this land from the wilderness left something behind, a tradition of service, discipline, and arms as a way of life. Our noble houses carry that tradition still. They do not merely own the land; they are sworn to defend it.

In Prussia, a commission is not purchased, it is owed. Our nobles are expected to lead, and to lead well. Men who grew up on the land know how to march across it, and how to keep their soldiers alive along the way.

Waging war cannot wait on the consent of our estates. We will establish a permanent organ of military finance, empowered to levy what the army requires. Our estates may not approve, but a well-funded army wins wars they cannot afford to lose.

Our court will not be a place of idle luxury. Every ducat saved is a ducat for the army; every hour wasted is a march not made. We ask nothing of our soldiers that we do not first demand of ourselves.

As we learned from the Persian invasion of Greece so long ago, a small army can defeat a larger one — as long as they have iron discipline and the proper training. We must elevate our own army to meet these extraordinary standards.

Every boy born in Prussia is born into a regiment. Each province will supply its own soldiers to its own officers, who will know their men by name. When war comes, we will not scramble to fill the ranks, they will already be there.

The Prussian Grenadiers are elite troops of the Prussian Army. Their role as vanguards in sieges and assaults requires them to be fearless fighters, recruited from among the strongest men in our country.

Other nations raise armies when war arrives and dismiss them when it ends. We cannot afford that luxury. Our army will be permanent, always trained, always ready, and the storehouses to sustain it will never run dry.

Most states are countries that have an army. Prussia, on the other hand, is an army that has a country! The many Kings of Prussia were soldiers as much as monarchs; each concluded their reign not only by reforming the state but also leaving a lasting impact on the army.

Auftragstaktik, or 'Mission Tactics'. is a system by which our subordinate leaders are informed about the objectives of the battle or the war by their commanders, and then are allowed to act on their personal initiative. This system allows our battalions to develop a tighter relationship with their leaders, yielding better results.

Shortcomings due to overconfidence and arrogance can lead to great failures and defeats. Defeat is a teacher, if we are willing to learn. We will purge our army of its complacency, noble birth alone will no longer open the officer ranks, and every soldier must understand not just his orders, but the purpose behind them.

Although it looks rather odd, the 'goose step' is specifically designed to facilitate our men holding their line as they advance towards the enemy. This provides our armies with a tangible advantage on the battlefield.

items.name: Pueblo
items.desc: Descendants of the ancestral Puebloans, the tribes of … have retained aspects of their ancestral ways despite having diverged into varying cultures. While we desire unification of these fractured tribes, this means we must contend with new cultural developments that have sprung up in individual pueblos. But these idiosyncrasies will make our union stronger and more unique, if we can find harmony.

items.name: Sardinia

c.t: Member of organization: Holy Roman Empire

items.desc: Our island has long been bitterly divided between our Judicates and foreign rulers. These dark times must end, and a ruler who unifies Sardinia shall govern us all, bringing peace and prosperity to our people... and war and devastation to our enemies. As they justly deserve.

adv.d: Our island was once divided into four self-governing judgedoms — the Giudicati — each with its own court, its own laws, and its own traditions of governance built entirely from within. Though that era has passed, the habits of independent administration it instilled run deep in our institutions and our people. This tradition of sovereign self-governance gives our state a legitimacy that is felt by every subject rather than merely proclaimed from above.

Our parliament, the Stamenti, is one of the oldest representative assemblies in the Mediterranean world, dividing legislative counsel among the church, the military nobility, and the royal towns in three distinct chambers. This structure gives every major constituency a recognized voice in how the island is governed, channeling disputes into procedure rather than conflict. This culture of structured representation keeps our merchant and burgher classes invested in the stability of the state.

The foundation of a university in our capital brings the institutions of learning that have long been enjoyed on the mainland to the people of our island. Lawyers, physicians, and administrators trained here no longer need to seek their education abroad, and the talent they represent stays in our service rather than enriching distant courts. This commitment to education raises the literacy and capability of our governing class and prepares our island for the demands of a more complex world.

Our foot soldiers have earned a reputation across the battlefields of the age for a tenacity that makes them exceptionally costly to break — they hold ground that others would abandon and press attacks that others would not dare. We formalize this tradition by organizing our infantry into disciplined formations trained in pike and shot, building on the fighting qualities that have always distinguished our men. This military culture produces an army of exceptional morale that serves as the backbone of any campaign we undertake.

The Sardinian interior, particularly the plains of the Campidano, has developed a world-class horse culture. The Sartiglia and other equestrian tournaments are not mere games, but displays of extreme horsemanship and military readiness. This culture will provide the state with elite light cavalry units (the Cavalleggeris de Sardigna) who are famous for their speed and ability to navigate the treacherous karst terrain, making them the premier scouts for our armies.

A generation of administrators has concluded that our potential has been constrained by outdated laws, uneven taxation, and a literacy gap that leaves too many of our subjects unable to participate in the life of the state. We commit to systematically reforming these institutions — codifying the tax rolls, expanding education, and replacing exemptions with a clearer and fairer legal framework. This administrative modernization increases our revenues and prepares our population for the demands of a transforming world.

items.name: Sardinia-Piedmont

c.t: Member of organization: Holy Roman Empire

items.desc: The union of the island of Sardinia with the mainland territory of Piedmont provides the perfect staging base from which to exert control over the rest of Italy and become one of the main forces in the Mediterranean.

items.name: Saxony
items.desc: The Duchy of Saxony was once an influential stem duchy within the old empire. While its core territories have shifted over time, the title has retained its prestige and renown. If we wish to be recognized as the rightful heir to the Saxon title, we must persuade the Emperor of the … to become an elector, a role which will be given to the Duke of Saxony.

adv.d: For centuries, mining has shaped our landscape, economy, and culture. Significant Silver discoveries in the region have attracted miners and traders from diverse regions, fostering the Ore Mountains' growth and expanding our realm's significance and development.

The Meißen Lion, also known as the Markmeißnische Löwe, holds a special place in heraldry. Representing the Wettin dynasty's symbol of power, an armored black lion with a red tongue gazes to the left on a golden field. Its image appears in various forms, including on painted tombstones, ensigns, helmets, coins, and seals, symbolizing the affiliation of the city of Meissen to the Mark Meißen and adorning the coats of arms of numerous towns and communities. Some link it to the recolored Thuringian lion.

Our people are truly resilient, embodying unwavering determination in the face of challenges. They weather adversity with unwavering spirit, finding strength in unity and a steadfast commitment to their shared values. Their indomitable resilience propels us forward, enabling us to overcome any obstacle that comes our way. We will always emerge stronger and more determined than ever before.

The Meißner groschen will serve as our national currency. This coin is based on the Prague groschen, which we will replace. This new large groschen will mark the beginning of a new era in the history of our coinage and will let us better control its influxes.

Religious infighting and intolerance plagues other lands, but we stand firm against allowing such strife to fester in our realm. Regardless of the diverse faiths our subjects hold, this nation shall be built on the strong pillars of tolerance and brotherhood, fostering a harmonious coexistence among all communities. United by a common vision, we will be forging a nation where respect and understanding flourish, paving the way for a prosperous future.

The Saxon Court is a pillar of Electoral Saxony's government, alongside civil and military administration. Court regulations define the responsibilities and daily routines of officials, while the court itself is composed of both nobles and peasants serving the ruling family in governance and administration. Traditionally, each adult member of the ruling family maintained their own household court, but we will now create a single, permanent court in our capital, attracting the finest minds in the realm.

Our valiant armies never waver! They demonstrate exceptional morale and loyalty, standing firm whether defending our realm or supporting allies. With indomitable spirits, they will press forward even in desperate circumstances, refusing defeat until physically unable to continue.

As the Reformation takes hold and the state assumes control over religious administration, a new responsibility arises for the emerging state: education, which was previously the duty of the Church. We will found princely schools at Pforta, Grimma, and Meissen using former monastic properties. Thus, the state will take on a significant role in shaping the educational landscape, fostering knowledge and intellectual growth for the future leaders of Saxony.
Saxony is the first country in Europe to produce Porcelain, which will bring wealth and prestige to the Wettin court.

Dresden and Leipzig, among other locales, have gained international recognition for being centers of Saxon Baroque culture. Magnificent architecture, like the Dresdner Hof, epitomize the grandeur of Saxony, while Johann Sebastian Bach's work has transformed Leipzig into a city of music and thriving highbrow culture. The region boasts unique expressions of culture, including handicrafts from the Ore Mountains and culinary traditions like the Dresdner Christstollen.

After tumultuous wars, a new era dawns upon Saxony — the remarkable Saxon Rétablissement. Amidst the ruins of our past, our nation will rise like a phoenix, rebuilding its shattered economy and charting a path toward prosperity. Driven by a blend of visionary state reforms and disciplined spending, our nation will emerge as a commercial hub. With unparalleled administrative prowess and a strategic focus on economic growth, this resolute transformation will mark a pivotal moment in history, shaping the destiny of Saxony well into the future.

Saxony's successful early industrialization is evident, with a highly developed industrial sector compared to other regions. The manufactory system, producing mainly for export, has flourished and will make Saxony a leading state in Germany's industrialization process. The emergence of smaller commercial landscapes and trade will be instrumental in promoting the region's economic growth and connections to other markets in Europe.

items.name: Scotland
items.desc: The once proud nation of Scotland has fallen into ruin. Yet, despite our shattered state, there remain some among the Clans with the will to restore our kingdom. We will muster our courage and fight for a free and independent Scotland!

adv.d: Now that our ties to England have been strengthened, we shall incorporate some of their military tactics, refining our units into fearsome forces.

c.t: Is or was the country Scotland (SCO)

adv.d: The clans of the Highlands have always moved and fought differently from lowland armies. Raised among the glens, lochs, and steep braes of the north, our clansmen are naturally comfortable engaging in terrain that would exhaust and disorient outsiders. This intimate knowledge of the local landscape is passed down from father to son, and no foreign conqueror has ever truly mastered it.

c.t: Is or was the country Balliol (SBL)
Is or was the country Scotland (SCO)

adv.d: Since the start of our war against English tyranny, we have preserved our independence through the valiant efforts of the courageous Scottish people. The memory of brave men like William Wallace will motivate our armies to defend and protect Scottish independence for all time!

c.t: Is or was the country Scotland (SCO)

adv.d: Our rivers and coastlines are rich in salmon. With careful attention and strict legislation, we will be able to harness this resource and shape our local economy towards export of this highly sought-after fish.
Securing peace with our southern neighbor has led to a steady influx of English aristocrats entering our administration. This makes it possible to exert our control over our country more effectively.

c.t: Is or was the country Scotland (SCO)

adv.d: Our country is situated at the far edge of Western Europe and is sparse in resources. If we are to thrive economically, we need to invest and expand our trade connections to further regions. The North Sea can connect us to rich markets and business opportunities, provided we learn to harness its potential.

War can be a long and tiring affair. If we are to defend our independence, we need to be prepared to endure hard times. Luckily, our people are as tenacious as the land they call their home, and resist foreign invaders to their last breaths.

c.t: Is or was the country Scotland (SCO)

adv.d: We have recently received a rather curious new tome. It is called On the True Significance of Comets against the Vanity of Astrologers, and it is positively filled with vital information on these highly suspicious entities. We have decreed that all in the realm should be aware of its contents.

c.t: Is or was the country Scotland (SCO)
Is or was the country Great Britain (GBR)
Is or was the country Isles (LOI)

adv.d: Since the Wars of Independence, we have been looking at reinforcing and updating our navy. Previously, we had used feudal obligations to bulk out our fleets with crew and ships, but we will now create a modern fleet, owned by the King and based in our port of Newhaven.

c.t: Is or was the country Scotland (SCO)
Is or was the country Great Britain (GBR)

adv.d: If Scotland is to continue its independent existence, we must secure stable sources of income. By tightening our control over the obligations owed to us by royal estates and feudal properties, we can increase our rightfully received taxes. Through these methods, we can ensure the Crown has sufficient funds to enact their will without relying on other sources of money.

c.t: Is or was the country Scotland (SCO)

adv.d: Having sent our brightest scholars to be educated in foreign universities for many years, it is time to improve our domestic education, and provide a place here in Scotland where the greatest minds of our nation can learn and grow. Our people should strive to acquire valuable knowledge and skills in their home country rather than wasting their money on expensive travel and their time on foreign institutions.

c.t: Is or was the country Scotland (SCO)
Is or was the country Great Britain (GBR)

adv.d: It has long been the custom to gift parts of the Royal Domain to our nobility as a reward for their services, but this system cannot be sustained if we want to ensure the integrity of our domain. From now on, we will insist on renting these lands instead of outright giving them away.

c.t: Is or was the country Scotland (SCO)

adv.d: Recruiting regiments from the people who live in the Scottish Highlands can be a crucial measure for our military efforts.

c.t: Is or was the country Scotland (SCO)

adv.d: For centuries, we relied on diplomacy and contact with foreign powers on the continent to ensure our independence. It is time to formalize this practice, and secure the endurance of our bonds for centuries to come.

u: Production method: Scottish Whisky Distillery Mills

c.t: Is or was the country Scotland (SCO)

adv.d: While distilleries have existed in Scotland for a long time, we should ensure these industries are finally put under the purview of the state. This supervision will allow us to establish ourselves at the forefront of liquor production, and expand our exports industry.

c.t: Is or was the country Scotland (SCO)

adv.d: Rapid advancements in philosophy, political economy, and medicine have led to a plethora of accomplishments by our fellow countrymen that will propel Scotland to the forefront of global innovation. This period of Scottish Enlightenment can be a very powerful tool for us on the world stage.

items.name: Serbia
items.desc: The Land of the Serbs has been divided and ruled by foreign powers for far too long, this is an insult to our national pride. Our people long to be ruled by one born among them. The path to unification is hard, but we must not rest until every city and settlement from the Danube to the southern mountains belongs to Serbia once more.

adv.d: We eagerly embrace the ways of Byzantium, aiming to mirror their laws and overall style. Drawing from the rich tapestry of Roman influences, we strive to infuse our governance and legal system with their essence, in a conscious effort to emulate the grace and sophistication of Byzantium within our realm.

The deliberate invitation of Sasi miners from Upper Saxony and the Harz Mountains has fundamentally transformed our primitive surface pits into sophisticated industrial engines. By granting these Germanic experts their own autonomous courts, the right to follow their own mining codes, and religious freedom, we have successfully unlocked the vast, deep-seated silver and gold veins of Brskovo and Novo Brdo. This influx of technical expertise provide us with the immense quantities of hard bullion necessary to hire the finest Western mercenaries, build monumental stone endowments, and mint the high-quality silver Matapan imitations that have come to dominate Balkan trade and Mediterranean commerce.

Our realm has developed various methods for swiftly amassing troops, so no enemy can catch us unprepared. This edge has helped us stand tall, despite all odds being against us, and we are prepared for battle. United, we march forward, resolute in purpose and ready to defend our honor and homeland!

We will encourage Viteštvo, a unique Serbian chivalric code, that will blend the heavy-armored traditions of the West with the stoic warrior-ethos of the East. This culture of knighthood will not be restricted to the highest nobility but trickle down into the lower classes of free soldiers. It will emphasize personal bravery, loyalty to the True Faith, and a specialized mastery of both the lance and the saber. This military culture will produce a population that is naturally predisposed to warfare, viewing military service as the highest form of social and spiritual achievement.

Serbia's rugged terrain has birthed a formidable network of defenses, epitomized by the imposing Smederevo Fortress. These enduring fortifications safeguard our nation, making invasion a daunting prospect. From the sprawling mountain ranges to the strategic river valleys, Serbia's defenses stand as a testament to our resilience and indomitable spirit.

In an era of conflict, the Serbian people turns to the pen to preserve what the sword can not. The Resava School of orthography will standardize the Serbian-Slavonic language, creating a cultural 'republic of letters'. This obsession with linguistic purity and the preservation of chronicles will ensure that Serbian history is never lost to the fog of war. It creates a highly literate elite who acts as the memory of the nation, keeping the records of our dynasties alive in every monastery scriptorium from the Danube to the Adriatic.

We will issue royal charters to the guilds of the Morava Valley, and encourage the development of large-scale leather-working, weaving, and metal-finishing workshops along the river's transit points. By exempting these guilds from certain internal tolls in exchange for providing standardized equipment to the royal armies — such as saddlery for the cavalry and uniforms for the infantry — the state will create a self-sustaining domestic industry. This move will reduce the realm's dependence on expensive foreign imports from outside and create a prosperous, urban middle class that serves as a loyal counter-weight to the rural power of the nobility, significantly broadening the state's taxable economic base.

Through incredible savvy and political maneuvering within the complex imperial administrative systems of our neighbors, we have successfully negotiated the restoration of our national Patriarchate. This diplomatic victory grants us spiritual and legal jurisdiction over all Serbian populations stretching from the Adriatic coast to the middle Danube, effectively allowing the Church to act as a 'Guardian of all Serbs'. It enables the maintenance of a shadow administration that collects tithes, manages local education, and keeps the flame of our traditions alive among a population that remains unified by a single, powerful faith.

Our realm has recognized the importance of fostering friendly relations and alliances with neighboring countries. To facilitate this, we will establish a specialized bureau dedicated to foreign affairs. By maintaining a dedicated focus on diplomacy, we are better positioned to navigate the complex web of international relations and secure our nation's prosperity.

Drawing from the hard-won experience of our veteran units of the previous decades, we have established a permanent, professional standing National Militia. This force represents a decisive move away from the disorganized peasant levy, utilizing rigorous Western drill, uniform equipment, and a modernized chain of command while retaining the fierce, high-morale fighting style of our Balkan predecessors. This ensures that our independence is not a fragile diplomatic gift, but is instead backed by a credible, modern military machine that can defend our borders against any encroaching imperial power.

Our people remember the birth of our nation: surrounded by formidable powers that pose permanent, looming threats to our security. This enduring vigilance has forged a culture of unwavering readiness, ensuring our armed forces stand as a shield against adversity. Fearless and respected, our soldiers have transformed us from potential prey to a mighty adversary, deterring any who dare encroach upon our sovereignty.

The Serbian peasantry has led its own cultural-economic revolution by adopting agrarian techniques learned from the West. This has turned the dense forests of Šumadija into a highly productive agricultural heartland. This surplus of food does not just feed the people; it fuels a demographic explosion. A well-fed Serbian population is a growing and ambitious one, providing a massive pool of young, healthy recruits for the army and a robust internal market that makes Serbia the dominant economic engine of the Central Balkans.

items.name: Silesia
items.desc: Silesia has been divided into Duchies and ruled from foreign capitals for centuries. Like jewels on a broken necklace, each part yearns to be restored to its whole and perfect state. Therefore, the hour has come for Silesia to cast aside foreign rule and quench the fires of internal division, creating a new, unified Silesian nation.

items.name: Somalia
items.desc: From the grasslands of …, to the sands of …, and even to the coasts of India, the … people have walked between many different worlds, and absorbed the many lessons these places had to teach us. But if we were to draw our people together as one, using the knowledge gained from such a cosmopolitan history, a united country for all … would be a powerful one.

items.name: Swabia
items.desc: After the decline of central power in …, no ruler was able to restore the old Swabia to its former strength, and the lands slowly fell into the grasp of foreign countries. Now, with large parts of … back under our control, we can finally rescue our legacy from the ashes of history and forge a new state.

items.name: Sweden
items.desc: The vast lands of Sweden were unified for centuries, and this union must be reaffirmed. With significant portions of the Swedish lands now under our control, we can finally revive this ancient legacy and once again claim a united Swedish nation.

adv.d: Forming our marching troops into a Svinfylking and charging is enough force to shatter any opponent! Mounted troops are not superior; other than being ridden to the battle itself, horses have no place on the battlefield.
Swedish peasants have always made significant contributions to our country; the differences between a noble and a free farmer have never been big.

b: Estate Satisfaction from Destroying Estate Buildings: -10%
adv.d: Swedish rulers often depended on cooperation with the estates, especially with such a large peasant class compared to that of the nobility. During the reign of Gustavus Adolphus, however, a historic compromise was made with the aristocrats, who loyally pledged their resources to the disposal of the nation in return for new privileges.

While other armies may be content to wildly fire inaccurate volleys at their enemies, we shall march at them in disciplined ranks, deliver a single volley at close range, and then feed them cold steel.

Swedish Iron, prized for its purity and strength, supplies not only our domestic needs but also the foundries and armories of nations across the continent. The Mulltimmer Masugn was not built just with stone, but also with wood isolated with sand, gravel and dirt.

The Kungliga Postverket, or Royal Postal Agency, was created to improve state administration and communication across the expanse of Sweden. It establishes a reliable network of couriers and waystations, and has become crucial for our military coordination, diplomacy, and governance.

The abundance of copper in Sweden, primarily from the Stora Kopparberget mine in Falun, has prompted the country to use it as the main metal for minting a new national currency, the daler. This is issued as a large money plate, called plåtmynt, which can weigh up to 20 kilograms. Some argue that this might not be very practical and that the volume of money in circulation could exceed copper reserves, but they seem narrow-minded.

The Caroleans are the Swedish and Finnish infantry of the Swedish Empire. Recruited from the peasantry, the Caroleans go under strict training and are renowned for invoking fear in the hearts of their enemies.

Finland is considered a rather poor and backwards region, but service in the Swedish cavalry offers skilled Finnish horsemen ample opportunities for glory and plunder. Superior horsemanship and high-quality mounts allow us to raise the feared Hakkapeliitta — cavalry so effective in battle that our enemies whisper they must be protected by witchcraft.
The Swedish allotment system divides the peasantry into groups of ten for recruitment purposes. This system made it easier to find people to serve in the army and organize them into units.

Christopher Polhem, dubbed the 'father of Swedish engineering, has transformed Swedish industry with his Machina Nova, an innovative array of mechanical systems designed to streamline and boost production. Using intricate systems of gears, cams, and water power, Polhem has developed several machines capable of performing tasks previously done by hand, from ore-crushing in mines to textile weaving and sawmilling.
Absolutism is the theory that one person should be in charge, that this person is the monarch, and that said monarch shall run the government unfettered by the Privy Council.
The decree forbids foreign ships arriving in Sweden to bring goods from countries other than their own or their colonies.
