items.desc: The … began as a mere alliance between different cantons. Each part has developed separately, speaking different languages and even having different laws. To truly unify the …, a sovereign power must establish dominance in the Swiss Plateau. While unifying so many different people will not be easy, we stand to gain much if we are successful.

items.name: Tibet
items.desc: The Tibetan Plateau was once united under a sprawling empire, which rivaled other great powers of its time for sophistication and wealth. However, over the centuries, that empire fell apart, irrevocably damaged by religious and political strife. But by bringing the … peoples together once again, we can revive our prodigal legacy and restore our lost kingdom.

adv.d: The Drokpa nomads often operate as herders and traders, porters that connect distant settlements. Through their traditions and unparalleled knowledge of the terrain, they traverse the high-altitude routes between Tibet, Bhutan, Ladakh, and Nepal. Their seasonal caravans carry Salt, Wool, and dried meat in exchange for grain and manufactured goods. These networks knit our mountains into a vibrant lattice of commerce and diplomacy.

A fusion of spiritual and temporal rule defines our political landscape. From the smallest village to the halls of power in Sakya, monastic institutions are central to every sphere of life. Their moral authority and organizational prowess ensure loyalty, unity, and cultural resilience.

For the last century, the Sakya school has held temporal authority over Tibet, acting as spiritual and political stewards under Mongol patronage. Their dominance ushered in an age of centralized governance and scholastic consolidation. Though their rule has waned, their legacy continues to shape our approach to authority and order.

Domesticated for centuries, the yak is the backbone of Tibetan pastoral life. It provides meat, milk, wool, transport, and fuel — even its dried dung is a vital source of fuel on the treeless plateau. In times of need or celebration, yak butter fills our lamps and cups.

Our monastic institutions have long served as centers of learning, debate, and spiritual discipline. Through rigorous training and a structured approach to education, our clerics maintain a high standard of intellectual and moral integrity. These foundations will support wise governance and cultural flourishing across our enlightened realm.

Sera, Ganden, and Drepung, these towering monastic universities form the intellectual heart of Tibet. Their scholars train one generation after another of monks, diplomats, and rulers. With their rise, our realm became not only a bastion of faith but a cradle of rigorous thought and institutional progress.

For centuries, our spiritual influence in China has formed the bedrock of our diplomatic relations. Imperial patronage, tribute exchanges, and sacred rituals like Tányuè secure both respect and material gain.

items.name: Transylvania
items.desc: 'The Lands Beyond the Forest' are rich with mineral resources and fertile farmlands, and populated by peoples of different origins — Vlachs, Magyars, and Germans — all of whom are proud of these lands they inhabit. From our capital, we will rule over this diverse group of newly-minted Transylvanian people, and bring prosperity to them all.

c.t: Is or was the country Transylvania (TRA)

adv.d: While Transylvania has remained part of the Hungarian Kingdom, the local Romanian, Saxon, and Hungarian nobles have all maintained a unique degree of regional autonomy under their own Voivode, and lived in peace. This shared governance has allowed everyone to preserve their distinct faiths and customs despite their apparent differences. This internal collaboration has ensured a certain degree of internal peace and multiculturalism in the Carpathian interior.

c.t: Is or was the country Transylvania (TRA)

adv.d: In response to threats of peasant revolts, our higher classes have formed the 'Union of the Three Nations'. This complex and rigid legal framework largely excludes the commoner majority, but creates a highly stable, fortified, and loyal administrative core for the region. This internal unity provides the crown with a reliable base of professional urban and feudal soldiers.

c.t: Is or was the country Transylvania (TRA)

adv.d: In the bustling cities of the Carpathian arc, merchants from our main cultural groups have begun to organize themselves into trade guilds and fraternities, often in competition or cooperation with the others. This is urbanizing a segment of the population, creating a middle class who funds schools and prints books. This economic rise will allow our nation to move beyond the village and into the marketplace of ideas and global commerce.

c.t: Is or was the country Transylvania (TRA)

adv.d: In a Europe increasingly torn apart by bloody and fanatical religious wars, Transylvania has bravely issued the Edict of Torda, the first law of universal religious tolerance in the Western world. By allowing Catholics, Lutherans, Calvinists, and Unitarians to coexist within a single legal framework, we have prevented the internal social collapse and civil strife seen throughout the Holy Roman Empire. This unprecedented religious peace makes our principality a safe haven for displaced scholars, scientists, and merchants, rapidly accelerating our adoption of modern administrative reforms and diverse cultural influences. Tolerance has become our greatest strategic asset.

c.t: Is or was the country Transylvania (TRA)

adv.d: As the age of gunpowder reaches its peak, we have adopted a unique school of military architecture that adapts the latest Italian and French Trace Italienne designs to the rugged, limestone geography of the Carpathian interior. Our major administrative centers have been refortified with low-profile, angled bastions capable of absorbing heavy siege artillery fire. Unlike the massive stone walls of the past, these modern earth-and-brick works are designed for active defense, featuring interlocking fields of fire for the principality's growing artillery corps. This defensive doctrine ensures that any invading army is bled dry in a series of prolonged, costly sieges before they can ever threaten the state's heartland.

c.t: Is or was the country Transylvania (TRA)

adv.d: We have established world-class scientific institutions to oversee the intensive extraction of gold, silver, and salt from the multiple mountain ranges of our nation. By applying the latest mineralogical and chemical techniques, we have turned Transylvania into the primary treasury of the region. This industrial focus has created a new class of professional engineers and technocrats who manage the state's resources with scientific precision, ensuring long-term economic stability.

items.name: Tuareg
items.desc: The veiled lords of the great desert have long ruled the dunes from oasis to oasis, masters of the caravan routes that link Agadez and Takedda to the salt pans of the north. Though our confederations have ever quarreled amongst themselves, a single banner raised over Tadmekka and Ghat would make us undisputed sovereigns of the Sahara.

adv.d: The legendary Tīn Hinān, founding ancestress of the Kel Ahaggar whose royal tomb at Abalessa we still tend, anchors a matrilineal inheritance custom that traces noble status, herd ownership, and ceremonial rank through the female line. Our amenokals each claim descent through their mother's clan from Tīn Hinān herself, and our succession disputes are settled in her cosmic authority. This matrilineal legitimacy binds our nobles to the throne through an inheritance system no patrilineal Maghrebi neighbor can disrupt or replicate.

Every caravan crossing our Saharan territory pays the Tuareg teggama protection tariff, at rates the amenokal's heralds publish at every waterpost, in exchange for safe passage past the raiding-clans of the deeper desert. Our escort detachments are drawn from every confederation through standing clan-oaths, and the tariff revenue circulates back through the same kin-network as redistribution to the tents that supplied the riders. This published-rate protection economy gives our crown a steady caravan-tariff revenue and a tribal cohesion that no settler-state can extract from our migration paths.

The Imūhagh, noble warriors mounted on the finest mehari and trained from boyhood in the lance, the cross-hilted takūba sword, and the iron-pointed javelin, form our striking-corps whose battlefield discipline no Sahelian army can answer. Their training-camps at the Ahaggar wells and the Aïr highlands instill an arms-mastery transmitted across generations. This noble-warrior tradition gives our confederation a light-cavalry striking force and an army-tradition recovery that any sedentary state would need centuries to reproduce.

The Inadan, an endogamous blacksmith-and-jeweller caste who serve every Tuareg confederation under reciprocal patronage contracts, work the silver crosses of Agadez, the takūba sword-blades, the inlaid leather amulet-boxes, and the iron-forged spear-and-knife tools that command premium prices across the Sahara. Our master smiths pass their techniques through hereditary apprenticeship within the caste, with the iron-forging and silver-jewellery skills concentrated in the same families across generations. This concentrated metalworking tradition gives our crown a silver-and-iron output that no sedentary Saharan power has been able to reproduce.

The mehari corps, riding the swift racing breed of camel rather than the slower baggage variety, sustains a deep-desert striking arm whose endurance no horse-mounted army can match across the dunes between the Aïr, the Ahaggar, and the Tassili. Our riders draw fresh mounts from every oasis well on the march, exchange wounded riders for fresh Imūhagh and Imghād warriors at every confederation camp, and return to camp with morale unbroken by losses no settler army would absorb. This elite mounted tradition gives our crown a battlefield morale recovery and a regiment reinforcement speed that the sedentary armies of the Sahel and the Maghreb cannot duplicate.

The litham veil of our nobles, the indigo-dyed robes that stain our men's skin blue, the Tifinagh-script poetry of our women, and the matrilineal customs that no neighboring people preserves — these markers of Tuareg identity persist under external pressures that have dissolved many other Saharan ethnoses. Our schools, our pasture-songs, and our marriage contracts transmit the inheritance unbroken across generations. This cultural continuity gives our crown a confederation-spanning administrative reach across the Saharan distances and an assimilation resilience that no centralizing empire can easily fragment.

items.name: Tunis
items.desc: Carthage, Rome, and the Hafsid caliphs have each ruled these shores in turn, leaving Kairouan's mosques and Tunis's harbors as monuments to a thousand years of empire. We are the rightful heirs to this inheritance, and we shall unite the coast, the Sahel, and the desert fringe beneath a single Tunisian crown. Let the memory of Ifriqiya's ancient glory guide us toward a sovereignty no rival Maghrebi power can equal.

adv.d: After the Mongol sack of Baghdad ends the 'Abbāsid line, our Hafsid sultans claim the khilāfa (the universal sovereignty over the Muslim community), invoking our Almohad-shayḵ descent and our role as protectors of Mālikī orthodoxy. Our Friday-sermons name our sultan as Commander of the Faithful, our coinage bears the caliphal titulature, and our diplomatic correspondence with the Mamluks, the Marinids, and the Ilkhanate insists on equal-sovereign protocol. This caliphal pretension gives the original Tunis line a religious-political authority that no other Maghrebi dynasty matches, neither Marinid, nor Zayyanid, nor Waṭṭāsid.

The Hafsid Ghulām are the slave-soldier corps of Hafsid Tunis: Black African captives from the trans-Saharan markets, Iberian prisoners from corsair raids, and children of earlier ghulām born to the institution and bound to the throne. They are the disciplined counterweight to the restless Banū Hilāl tribal levies.

The corsair captains of Tunis and La Goulette have hunted Christian shipping in the central Mediterranean since the late Hafsid century, operating under state charter alongside Christian renegades, Greek captains turned Muslim, and adventurers from every Mediterranean port who find refuge and employment in our service. Our shipyards at Bizerte and Porto Farina maintain the swift ṣḵīrah galleys that both native and foreign-recruited captains employ, and the slave markets at Tunis re-export captives across the Maghreb and into the Ottoman world. This state-sponsored privateering, drawing on both Tunisian-born and renegado talent, gives Tunis a fleet of effective war-galleys and a sailor pool that no Maghrebi treasury could otherwise afford to maintain.

The Hafsid sultans have maintained continuous commercial and diplomatic relations with Pisa, Genoa, Venice, Aragon, and Provence since the thirteenth century, signing successive capitulations that grant European merchants resident factors at Tunis and La Goulette. Our court receives Christian envoys with the same protocol that we extend to fellow Muslim sovereigns, and our customs revenue from Italian trade alone funds a third of the central treasury. This pragmatic engagement with Christian Europe gives Tunis a commercial and diplomatic flexibility that the more isolationist Maghrebi states lack.

The Tunis court of our sultans patronizes 'Abd ar-Raḥmān ibn Khaldūn during his formative years (the philosopher-historian whose Muqaddima lays the foundations of social-historical analysis a century before any European parallel), alongside the wider circle of Andalusi refugee scholars, North African qadi-historians, and visiting Eastern ulama who pass through our capital. Our court librarians compile the genealogies, our administrative archives preserve the chancery records that later historians draw on, and our patronage of Ibn Khaldūn's contemporaries makes Tunis a magnet for scholarly correspondence across the Muslim world. This Khaldunid intellectual flowering gives the original Tunis line a cultural patrimony that no other Maghrebi court can claim for the period.

The bey holds Crown monopolies on the export of olive oil, woolen textiles from Sfax, henna and indigo Dyes, and the dried fish of the Tunisian banks, all staples that no Mediterranean market can fully replace from elsewhere. Our state warehouses concentrate these goods before they reach foreign factors, and our pricing committees set rates that Italian and Provençal buyers must accept or do without. This system of crown export monopolies funds the central treasury with a stable foreign-currency income that fluctuating caravan revenues cannot match.

Our hegemony stretches across the Ifrīqiyan axis (Tunis, Bougie, Constantine, Tripoli) administered through a network of governor-cousins, tribute-paying Banū Hilāl tributaries, and resident Christian-merchant factor-houses whose customs revenue funds the central treasury. Our distance-administration relies on signal-towers along the coast, paid couriers on inland routes, and a customary code that grants regional governors broad latitude in exchange for promptly-remitted tribute. This Tunis-Bougie-Tripoli administrative axis gives the original Tunis line an imperial reach across Ifrīqiya that no successor regime fully restores.

Our state shipyards at Bizerte and Porto Farina come under formal beylical-admiralty command: replacing the personal-charter corsair captain with a salaried fleet officer, organizing the conscription of sailors from the Sahel coastal towns through a registered ship-roll, and substituting heavier galley-and-galleon classes for the lighter raiding vessels that the previous century relied on. Our naval academy at La Goulette trains its officer cadre in the gunnery and navigation that the Mediterranean wars now demand, and our paymasters disburse fleet wages from the central treasury rather than through prize-share. This state-organized naval administration gives our successor regimes a fleet that no personal-charter corsair tradition could sustain through the gunpowder era.

Our state navy and our garrison at La Goulette resist the successive Habsburg-Ottoman intrusions that the gunpowder Mediterranean brings: Khayr ad-Dīn Barbarossa's first occupation, Emperor Charles V's restoration of our sultan, and the long war of attrition that follows. Our chief admirals and our Tunis qasba commanders fortify the harbor's seaward approaches, our court diplomats play the rival empires against each other to preserve dynastic autonomy, and our resident Andalusi engineers redesign our cannon batteries to the latest specifications. This Hafsid anti-imperial defense gives the original Tunis line a defensive military patrimony that successor regimes can draw on as institutional inheritance.

Our Husaynid beys claim direct dynastic-legitimacy succession from the original Hafsid line, citing genealogical chains compiled by our court scholars, ceremonial titulature preserved across the Ottoman-regency interregnum, and the formal continuity of palace office that the Bardo administrators trace back through the deys to the last Hafsid sultans. Our investiture ceremonies, our diplomatic credentials, and our court-historians' chronologies all affirm this Hafsid-Husaynid continuity as the foundation of our legitimacy. This genealogical succession-claim gives the original Tunis line a dynastic patrimony that no rival regency can match for old-dynasty legitimacy.

Our dynasty, founded by Ḥusayn ibn 'Alī (an officer of Cretan-Anatolian descent risen through the deylical hierarchy), consolidates the bey's authority over the Janissary corps, the dey, and the pasha, replacing the rotating-officer governance of the prior generations with a hereditary line. Our successive beys appoint mamluk advisors trained from boyhood in the Bardo Palace, our administrative reforms centralize the tax-farms under direct beylical control, and our diplomatic correspondence with Istanbul recognizes Ottoman sovereignty in form while exercising autonomous power in fact. This dynastic consolidation gives our polity a coherent administrative continuity that no rotating-officer regime could supply across generations.

Our reformist circles revive the Hafsid caliphal-memory as an ideological resource, citing the centuries when Tunis was the western caliphal capital, the Ifrīqiyan hegemony that our forerunners maintained from Constantine to Tripoli, and the universal-sovereignty claims that distinguished our ancestors from any contemporaneous Maghrebi dynasty. Our pamphleteers invoke the precedent against the encroaching foreign centers of authority, our official histories foreground the Hafsid caliphal era over the intervening centuries, and our modernist ulama trace our reform program's legitimacy through this restored caliphal lineage. This dynastic-memory revival gives the original Tunis line an ideological patrimony that purely-modernist reform movements elsewhere lack.

The 'Ahd al-Amān (the security pact that our bey proclaims under reformist pressure) guarantees equality before the law for Muslims, Christians, and Jews, the inviolability of person and property under judicial process, and the formal codification of taxation and conscription procedures that the prior regimes left to discretionary practice. Our reformist drafters, drawing on Tanzimat and European precedents but framing the document in classical Arabic-Islamic legal terms, secure its endorsement from both the Zaytuna ulama and the Bardo court. This pre-modern constitutional document gives our polity a legal framework that the unreformed Maghrebi and Ottoman peers cannot match from custom-and-decree governance alone.

items.name: Valencia
items.desc: The Kingdom of Valencia was carved from the Muslim taifas by the Aragonese reconquest, and its huertas have grown wealthy under our care. By securing the whole of Valencia for our crown, we shall at last be a kingdom in our own right rather than a junior partner of the Aragonese crown.

adv.d: The Llibre del Repartiment — the master register of lands, orchards, and houses assigned to the Christian repopulators after the 1238 conquest of Balansiya by Jaume I — fills page upon page with plots distributed among settlers from Catalonia, Aragon, Navarre, and southern France. This book will remain the definitive title document for centuries to come, cited in inheritance disputes and royal grants alike, and establishing the agrarian property regime of the entire kingdom from the first decade of Christian rule. This authoritative land record raises the productive ceiling of every Valencian estate and frees our peasantry from the boundary disputes that plague less well-surveyed realms.

The first printing press in the Iberian Peninsula was installed at Valencia by the German master Lambert Palmart, who issued the Obres e trobes en lahors de la Verge Maria — a volume of Marian verse composed for a literary prize — as the inaugural book of Hispanic typography. From that workshop the trade spread rapidly: Spindeler, Hagenbach, and Rosenbach established their own shops at Valencia within twenty years, producing Bibles, legal compendia, and the great chivalric prose of Tirant lo Blanch. This printing primacy seeds workshops across the kingdom and gives our culture a head start in the diffusion of texts that other Spanish realms must purchase from us.

The germanies of Valencia — sworn brotherhoods of weavers, dyers, blacksmiths, and the dozens of other guilded trades that fill our city walls — extend beyond their craft business into mutual-aid funds, militia musters, religious processions, and parish welfare. Membership in a germania is the central social identity of an urban Valencian alongside parish and family, and the brotherhoods provide the trained levies and ready supply chains the Crown calls upon in every campaign. This dense fraternal infrastructure gives our towns manpower reserves and civic discipline that more atomized urban populations cannot easily replicate.

Our silk industry — the seda valenciana — clusters in the parish of Velluters and around the Albufera, drawing on mulberry groves planted across the Vall d'Albaida and Vall de Càrcer to feed the silkworm hatcheries each spring. The Col·legi de l'Art Major de la Seda regulates the looms, sets quality standards, and apprentices new weavers under masters whose lineages reach back to the Morisco artisans the kingdom never wholly displaced. This vertically integrated silk complex — orchard, hatchery, reeling shed, and loom — gives our Crown a luxury-cloth output no other Iberian region can match.

adv.n: Real Societat Econòmica d'Amics del País
adv.d: The Real Societat Econòmica d'Amics del País of Valencia draws together our enlightened nobility, parish clergy, and burgher reformers around the patient improvement of irrigation, livestock, manufactures, and primary schooling across the kingdom. The society funds prize competitions for the best designs of looms and water-lifting devices, sponsors translations of foreign agronomic treatises, and dispatches expert correspondents to every village willing to host them. This dedicated reform institution channels enlightened patronage into measurable improvements in the productive capacity and revenue base of our Crown.

Our literary revival — the Renaixença Valenciana — gathers around the restored Jocs Florals of Valencia and around the pastoral lyric, the verse satire, and the historical chronicles that re-emerge from the printing presses of our kingdom. We will channel royal and municipal patronage to the prize medallions of the Floral Games and the new Valencian journals, restoring our tongue to a literary stage worthy of the libraries of cultivated households across the realm. This linguistic renewal raises the prestige of our court and binds our scattered comarques into a shared cultural community no foreign administration can easily fragment.

items.name: Wales
items.desc: Free from the influence of faraway rulers, the Welsh people will establish their own state, governing themselves without the intervention or consent of others. Like the great red dragon of legend, the Welsh will emerge triumphant from the throes of conflict!

adv.d: The powerful martial longbow, originally deployed with great impact against armored English knights in the Welsh valleys, has been adopted into the military doctrine on either side of the border.

adv.d: The Longbowmen excel not only due to their powerful warbow but also their years of training on the archery fields.

adv.d: Small innovations in equipment and organization result in continuous devastating volleys that shatter all but the most heavily armored formations.

items.name: Westphalia
items.desc: Our people were once held in thrall by severe religious oppression, but we have seen a new way — a better way — a way that will allow us to become a fully realized nation at last. As these religious influences slowly fade into the past, we shall form a new state for … and proclaim the dawning of a new era for our people.

items.name: Aïr
items.desc: The mountains of … have served as refuge for the … peoples for centuries, an island of green amidst the sand dunes of the desert. This area is rich in resources and well-fortified, making it a perfect stronghold from which to command our new nation. With our people finally united as one, these mountains will serve as the first step on our quest for expansion.

items.name: Beja
items.desc: Our people have traditionally been divided among several clans and families, some powerful enough to call themselves kingdoms. However, their apparent strength is in actuality extremely fragile. Only a realm that unites all clans under a single banner can bring true power and prosperity to our people!

items.name: Bulgaria
items.desc: The Kingdom of Bulgaria fought for its own survival for centuries, constantly hounded by attacks from its covetous neighbors. It has fallen once, been resurrected, and then again crumbled. But with our steady hand to guide them, the people of Bulgaria will finally rise again as one nation, and this time, achieve the status of a major global empire!

adv.d: The reign of Ivan Asen II marked a new height of Bulgarian power, diplomacy, and economic expansion. His legacy endures as a foundation for a strong and centralized state.

The capital of Tarnovo, perched upon the cliffs of Tsarevets and Trapezitsa, is arguably the most formidable fortress in the Balkans, symbolizing the power of the Asen dynasty. By continuously expanding the complex of palaces, patriarchal cathedrals, and triple-layered walls, we have created an administrative center that is immune to sudden coups or sieges. This architectural dominance projects an image of imperial stability that cowers the local Boyars and convinces the populace that the 'Third Rome' has truly moved to the banks of the Yantra.

At its peak, the chancellery in Tarnovo was the most sophisticated diplomatic hub in the Orthodox world, producing intricate Slavic charters that influenced the courts of Serbia and Russia. By professionalizing the class of Logothetes and scribes, the Tsars will ensure that every land grant and international treaty is meticulously recorded and legally binding. This administrative rigor will allow the state to extract taxes more efficiently and manage its complex network of vassalage with a degree of central control that is rare in the late medieval period.

Under the direct patronage of the Shishman Dynasty, the nation has undergone a spectacular cultural growth, positioning itself as a true Third Rome and the primary guardian of Orthodox high culture. By funding the reconstruction of the Patriarchal Cathedral and the royal palaces of Tsarevets, the state has gathered a new generation of master iconographers, hagiographers, and architects who blend traditional Byzantine aesthetics with a unique, emotive Bulgarian realism. This school of thought does not merely produce religious icons; it serves as a powerful instrument of imperial propaganda, codifying the Bulgarian recension of Church Slavonic and producing the Manasses Chronicle to legitimize the Tsar's claim to the Byzantine heritage.

To prevent the internal strife that plagued the 14th century, we will evolve into a 'Consultative Autocracy' where the most powerful Boyars are integrated into a permanent State Council. This body will serve as a high court and a military planning board, ensuring that the interests of the landed nobility are aligned with those of the crown. This political stability will allow us to maintain a large standing army and avoid the devastating civil wars that have historically left the empire vulnerable to its neighbors.

The spiritual teachings of Grēgórios Sinaítēs have moved from the hermit's cell to the halls of power. By adopting Hesychasm — a philosophy of inner stillness and divine light — as the unofficial state ideology, we foster a populace that is deeply pious and resilient. This shared spiritual identity acts as a powerful deterrent against the influences from our enemies, making the Bulgarian subjects immune to foreign conversion or subversion.

Drawing on the iron mines of the Balkan mountains and the expertise of Saxon miners, we will establish the first major domestic gunpowder industry in the region. These foundries will produce heavy siege cannons and early handguns, allowing the Bulgarian army to transition away from purely feudal cavalry toward a more modern, infantry-heavy force. By controlling the production of saltpeter and iron, we will ensure that our walls remain the most dangerous obstacle for any would-be conqueror in the Balkans.

Utilizing the fertile Thracian plains and the unique climate of the Rose Valley, we have established state-protected guilds for the production of luxury oils and silk. These high-value, low-weight goods are perfect for overland export to the courts of Europe and Asia. The wealth generated by these guilds allows the state to build a massive gold reserve, making our economy one of the most stable and credit-worthy in the entire Mediterranean basin.

adv.n: The Grand Academy of the Yantra
adv.d: The intellectual legacy of the 14th-century Tarnovo Literary School is revived in the 17th century through the creation of a modern state university. This institution focuses on civil law, engineering, and the translation of Western scientific texts into the Bulgarian vernacular, creating a class of bureaucrats who are as capable as any in Paris or Vienna. This modernization of the elite will ensure that we can manage a complex, multi-ethnic empire while maintaining the cultural purity of its Bulgarian core.

Moving away from seasonal levies, we have established the first permanent 'Regiments of the Lion'. These infantrymen are trained year-round in the use of firearms, following a rigorous drill based on the successes of neighbor models but adapted for Balkan terrain. This professional infantry core give us a reliable tool for offensive warfare, capable of out-marching and out-shooting the traditional armies of our neighbors.

Knowledge is power. We have instituted a decennial census that records every person, unit of livestock, and hearth in the empire. This precise data allows for the most efficient taxation and conscription system in the Balkans. By knowing exactly what the nation can provide, we can plan long-term campaigns with a level of logistical certainty that ensures our armies are always well-fed and our coffers never empty.

We have fully embraced our role as the natural leader of the Balkan peoples, articulating a formal doctrine for the reunification of all former Bulgarian lands. This fate is backed by a modern, professionalized army and a sophisticated diplomatic corps that seek to play the Great Powers against one another. The belief in a 'Greater Bulgaria' becomes the central pillar of the state, driving a policy of aggressive expansion and cultural assimilation that seeks to restore the empire of Simeon the Great.

items.name: Circassia
items.desc: The division of the Circassian people into separate competing tribes must end. If we wish to grow strong and not succumb to external pressure, we must be brought together under a single powerful leader who can skillfully guide our people towards prosperity — and strike terror deep in the hearts of our enemies.

c.t: Is or was the country Circassia (CIR)

adv.d: Our lands have again and again been raided by foreign powers, and our people enslaved. Some of these slaves, used as soldiers, have advanced in their new lives, accumulating power and wealth of their own. With some convincing, we could convince them to return to our lands, and protect it from future invasions.

c.t: Is or was the country Circassia (CIR)

adv.d: We will elect a nominal leader of our people, who will act as our representative but will not meddle with the oversight of local lords.

c.t: Is or was the country Circassia (CIR)

adv.d: Our settlements lie unprotected, and are easy prey to any invader. As these settlements grow, however, we can directly incorporate the hilly terrain into our defensive lines, enhancing their protection. If necessary, we can even create the elevated terrain required ourselves.

c.t: Is or was the country Circassia (CIR)

adv.d: Our position at the edge of the steppes has resulted in multiple mounted invasions of our homelands. If we want to ensure our independence, we will need to raise a great host ourselves, and expand our influence over the steppes, securing our heartland.

c.t: Is or was the country Circassia (CIR)

adv.d: To unify our people, we shall elect the greatest of our lords as the Grand Prince, who will serve as an inspiring leader for our troops.

c.t: Is or was the country Circassia (CIR)

adv.d: Our lands are frequented by many Catholic, Muslim, and Orthodox people, who frequently engage in trade with our population. We should foster a collective tolerance between all our subjects, to promote peace and stability.

items.name: Connacht
items.desc: One of the traditional kingdoms of …, Connacht boasts a long and storied history. Having gained enough influence to obtain High Kingship over the whole island, Connacht has a certain claim to tradition and leadership — but whether we will be able to stand firm in the face of would-be oppressors or not depends on our unification.

items.name: Dalmatia
items.desc: Dalmatia has traditionally been a region dominated by foreigners, as its coasts, islands, and bays are all paramount to dominating the extremely lucrative … trade routes. But why should foreigners reap the benefit of Dalmatia, when her own people deserve her riches far more? It is finally time to shake off foreign control of the region and establish an independent Dalmatia!

adv.d: To secure the loyalty of the coastal cities against Venetian encroachment, we will issue privileges that guarantee the internal autonomy and Latin laws of those comunes (a unit of government). By allowing these cities to elect their own priors and manage their own local taxes, we create a loyal urban class that views us as a protector rather than an oppressor. This decentralized urban defense ensures that the coast is a patchwork of loyal, fortified comunes that can hold out against maritime raids, bringing the coasts and inner lands together.

adv.n: The Union of the Two Souls
adv.d: The Dalmatian culture has matured into a truly bilingual society where Latin is the language of the law and Slavic is the language of the heart. This linguistic flexibility allows our people to navigate the complex social strata of the Renaissance Adriatic with ease. By mastering both tongues, our merchants and sailors become the indispensable intermediaries for all trade between the Italian city-states and the Slavic interior. This bilingualism creates a 'Dalmatian Bridge' culture that is uniquely adapted to international trade and diplomacy, ensuring that our people are always at the center of Mediterranean commerce.

As we consolidate our rule, we have turned our population into the 'Sword of the Nation'. Our men are recruited into elite Schiavoni (Slavic) regiments, serving as the frontline heavy infantry for our wars. This military service provides our people with professional training and exposure to the latest European warfare techniques, creating a culture of career soldiers. While our cities may lose their mercantile edge, our people become the most respected warriors in the Mediterranean, ensuring that our military tradition remains unbroken even under foreign administration.

Recognizing that the Mediterranean is becoming a sea of fire, we have commissioned a new class of heavy, oak-reinforced oared vessels built in our best shipyards. By utilizing the iron-hard timber of the coastal mountains, these ships can withstand heavier broadsides and are designed to navigate the shallow, rocky karst inlets where large Venetian galleys founder. This superiority allows us to police our own waters and defend our coasts from any enemy.

We have integrated the Morlachs — the fierce Vlach and Slavic shepherds of the interior — into a permanent military reserve. These irregulars are granted land rights in exchange for constant readiness, serving as the eyes and ears of the nation. Their intimate knowledge of the karst geography allows us to conduct deep-strike ambushes and night raids that paralyze the enemy's logistics. This creates a 'Nation in Arms' culture in the Dalmatian hinterland, where the boundary between civilian and soldier is entirely erased in the name of our defense.

We have pivoted our economy toward intensive agriculture, taking advantage of the climate of the Dalmatian coast. By establishing state-monitored 'Agricultural Pacts', we have reclaimed the coastal hills for large-scale production, turning our rugged land into a green garden of exports. This economic diversification reduces our reliance on the maritime trade and provides a new source of wealth for the coastal nobility, funding the construction of grand summer villas and urban theaters that rival those of the Italian mainland.

items.name: Finland
items.desc: Over the centuries, the … people have been ruled by foreign powers, and their lands controlled by foreign hands. But we have never lost our distinct Finnish ways nor our desire to subdue those who would oppress us for them, and our moment to break away is finally here. The time has come for the state of Finland to be born and take its place among the pantheon of nations!

adv.d: Swedish Iron, prized for its purity and strength, supplies not only our domestic needs but also the foundries and armories of nations across the continent. The Mulltimmer Masugn was not built just with stone, but also with wood isolated with sand, gravel and dirt.

Finland is considered a rather poor and backwards region, but service in the Swedish cavalry offers skilled Finnish horsemen ample opportunities for glory and plunder. Superior horsemanship and high-quality mounts allow us to raise the feared Hakkapeliitta — cavalry so effective in battle that our enemies whisper they must be protected by witchcraft.

items.name: Gilan
items.desc: Situated on the shores of the … and in the heart of …, Gilan has existed under the shadow of … for centuries. The time has come for us to establish its presence on the world stage, and emerge as an independent power.

items.name: Iceland
items.desc: Circumstances have led to our holdings in … developing into the foremost part of our country. Let us embrace this new identity and establish the nation of Iceland. We shall strengthen our local institutions, firmly entrenching our right to rule over the island and bringing our people together at last.

items.name: Kazakh
items.desc: Across the windswept expanse of the steppes, the … people roam free without a unifying ruler, leaving us vulnerable to outside attacks. But were we to finally be brought together under the command of a single leader, and to share an identity as a nation, we could turn the tide. Thus, we shall unite under one flag to rule the seas of grass as mighty Kazakh.

items.name: Livonia

pot.t: Any primary, accepted or tolerated culture:

items.desc: The lands of Curonia, Livonia, and Estonia were once part of the Livonian Order, who swore to convert their conquered territories to …. While the Order built a functioning state, it did so on the backs of the very people it had conquered, who planted seeds of resentment alongside their crops. Should the Order fail to uphold the order of society, they would be easy enough to replace with a bit of force and Livonian courage.

adv.d: The many fortifications in our territories owe their construction and funding to our numerous Crusader bands. Flanked by sturdy walls, these fortifications will serve and protect our people for years to come!

Our nation is founded on the strong backs of the brave Christian men who have joined our order as knights. Their martial prowess will compensate for our low numbers, compared to those of the Pagans surrounding us, as will the light and strength of our faith.

The knights of our order have proven their valor and skill in battle time and time again. By promoting the most capable among them to bannerets, we ensure that our armies will always be led by the best.

items.name: Mazovia
items.desc: Despite being one of the major … cultures, the Mazovians are culturally and linguistically distinct from other … groups. Given this, it seems fitting for our people to demand the unification of all Mazovian lands under a single ruler, as only that way will we be able to fully demonstrate our unique power and glory to the world.

items.name: Meath
items.desc: Meath was once counted among the great provinces of Ireland, a kingdom whose kings held sway over much of Leinster and whose territory encompassed the ancient seat of Tara. By consolidating our hold over these lands, we can restore that ancient legacy and reclaim the kingdom's rightful place among the realms of Ireland.

items.name: Mecklenburg
items.desc: With the unification of the Mecklenburgian territories, we can create a new, independent Dukedom within northern Germany. This new state will be able to undo the mistakes of the past, avoiding the fracturing of our territories into multiple sovereign countries and creating a counterbalance to the rivals who covet our lands.

items.name: Moldavia
items.desc: For too long, the Moldovans have lived under different warlords, who in turn were subjects of more powerful rulers. But now the moment has come to supplant these odious middlemen and crush the rule of our oppressors! It is time to reunite our people under the banner of the Bull, and ensure the bright and independent future of our nation.

c.t: Is or was the country Moldavia (MOL)

adv.d: By securing the 'Moldavian Road' connecting the Baltic Sea to the Black Sea, we have positioned our main settlements as vital hubs for the Northern European fur and wax trades. We have granted extensive privileges to Slavic merchants and German burghers to settle in our customs towns, ensuring that every caravan passing from the Baltic to the Genoese ports of the south pays a heavy toll into our treasury. This commercial wealth allows us to fund a professional court and to build stone fortifications without taxing our free peasantry into rebellion.

adv.n: The Banner of the Golden Bull

c.t: Is or was the country Moldavia (MOL)

adv.d: Under the banner of the Golden Bull, representing our nation, Moldavia will become the 'Bulwark of the East', successfully defending against enemy incursions. We will start a tradition of building a monastery for every military victory that will create a landscape of religious sites. This fusion of religious zeal and military discipline ensures our soldiers fight with the conviction of crusaders.

c.t: Is or was the country Moldavia (MOL)

adv.d: To counter the numbers of our enemies, we have reorganized our army into the Oastea Mare (The Great Army). By granting land to the Răzeși — free-holding peasants who owe service directly to the Voivode — we have created a loyal, self-equipped infantry core that fights with the ferocity of landowners defending their own soil. This system ensures that even when the boyars waver, the Prince has a reliable and massive pool of battle-hardened soldiers.

c.t: Is or was the country Moldavia (MOL)

adv.d: A transformative era of intellectual self-awareness has dawned! Our high boyars have begun to systematically document the history of our people in our native Romanian for the first time. By scientifically documenting the Latin origins and linguistic heritage we share with our Romanian brothers, we shift the state's foundation from a purely religious identity to a modern linguistic and historical one. This cultural awakening strengthens the internal legitimacy of the Prince and provides our diplomats with the historical arguments needed to assert our sovereignty among the European courts. History has become a weapon of the state.

c.t: Is or was the country Moldavia (MOL)

adv.d: Dimitrie Cantemir has ascended to become a polymath of European renown, bringing the radical principles of the early Enlightenment directly into our court. By mapping the intricate history, music, and geography of our region for a Western audience, we have gained a profound strategic advantage in the shifting sands of Eastern European politics. We have transitioned from a medieval frontier march into a scientifically managed state that looks increasingly toward the modernized reforms of the West for its political and military inspiration. Knowledge is the new currency of the Moldavian throne.

c.t: Is or was the country Moldavia (MOL)

adv.d: Vineyards have remained Moldavia's greatest treasure, with the sweet white wines of Cotnari rivaling Tokay in the courts of Europe. We have already codified the first wine classifications, establishing a state interest in the export of 'Perle de la Moldavie'; now it is time to pass to action. This luxury trade will provide the Princely court with significant hard currency from neighboring markets, funding the lavish palaces in our capital.

items.name: Mossi
items.desc: We are a people deeply devoted to our unique beliefs and traditions, proud of our political acumen and military strength. Yet despite our deeply ingrained culture, our people have failed to unify as a single group, and the consequences of that division have been dire. Only through unity can our people find peace and enjoy prosperity — we must achieve it!

items.name: Munster
items.desc: Munster, the great southern province of Ireland, was home to kings such as Brian Boru who once claimed the high kingship of the whole island. With Munster's fertile lands and Atlantic harbours under our banner, we shall revive this ancient kingdom and stand as masters of the south.

items.name: Nassau
items.desc: Although the Duchy of Nassau was neither the most stable nor the most famous of its peers, our founding dynasty connects us to many crowned heads of …, giving us a strong position from which to claim authority. To make our voice within Germany heard, we must unify the lands of Nassau once and for all and reassert the strength of this dynastic legacy, preventing any further fracturing of our rightful territory.

u: Chivalric order: Society with the Lion
adv.d: Founded in the woes of the Western Schism, the Löwenbund is sworn to protect our lands from heretical revolts. We should grant them our official sponsorship and incorporate them into our court to further our cause.

items.name: Northumberland
items.desc: For too long, the lands of the Northumbrians have been governed by southerners or people from across the sea. It is time for us to take the reins of our nation and reclaim the glory our ancestors once knew. The lords of the North shall rise once more!

items.name: Thessalonica
items.desc: A short-lived … established by the crusaders in … in the aftermath of the Fourth Crusade, its rulers wielded great influence in the …. While it was destroyed by … in 1224, should we manage to reclaim its contested territories, it would make us a considerable power in ….

adv.d: Boniface of Montferrat, crowned King of Thessalonica in 1204, established a northern Latin kingdom that controlled the vital Via Egnatia and much of Macedonia, creating a wealthy and strategically important realm whose capital became a glittering center of Frankish court life, Italian commerce, and Orthodox–Catholic coexistence under Latin domination. Although repeatedly threatened by surrounding enemies, the kingdom's barons maintained a proud martial tradition and a flourishing economy based on grain, wine, and transit trade, ensuring that Thessalonica remained one of the brightest jewels in the Frankokratia.

We have expanded the ancient religious fair into a massive international trade expo that links the Balkan hinterland with the Mediterranean maritime routes. By granting safe passage to merchants, Thessalonica has become the premier marketplace for fur, grain, and Western textiles. This economic vitality allows the King to bypass the local nobility by funding his administration through sales taxes and customs duties.

Restored as a bulwark in Macedonia, the Kingdom has revived its heritage by inviting Lombard and northern Italian military engineers to modernize its defenses. These Lombard Guards serve as the professional core of the army, utilizing advanced pike-and-shot formations to hold the Vardar valley against the encroaching enemy armies. Their presence ensures that our nation remains a bastion of Western military theory in the heart of the Balkans.

The King has commissioned the total resurfacing and fortification of the ancient Via Egnatia, the vital artery connecting the Adriatic to the Bosporus. By establishing permanent garrisons along this road, we have eliminated banditry and drastically reduced the travel time for both merchants and armies. This logistical masterpiece cements Thessalonica as the indispensable bridge between the Latin Empire and the Western European powers.

Our hunters have tapped into the vast wilderness of the northern mountains, establishing a lucrative trade in high-quality pelts for the luxury markets of Italy and France. By regulating the trapping seasons and protecting the trade routes to the Danube, we have secured a consistent source of 'furry gold' for the royal treasury. This industry funds the modernization of our northern fortifications against the rising power of the northern principalities.

Thessalonica has founded a royal university dedicated to the study of a diverse array of matters, blending Italian theory with local Balkan experience. This institution produces the finest students in the Frankokratia, capable of marvels. Our graduates are in high demand across the Latin world, making the Kingdom the intellectual center of innovation.

items.name: Tuscany
items.desc: The ancient March of Tuscany endured for centuries, but after the death of their ruler Matilda of Canossa in 1115, it eventually faded away. Its former territory was carved up and claimed by various ascendant urban communes, and the memory of a united Tuscany faded into darkness. But circumstances have changed, and it may now be time to reunite our dispersed lands and people under one rule again.

adv.d: The Contado — the ring of rural territory surrounding each of our cities — has long been the foundation of Tuscan wealth and power, its villages, castles, and farmlands bound by law and custom to answer to the urban lord within the walls. By formalizing our jurisdiction over the countryside, we transform scattered feudal obligations into a coherent system of agricultural surplus, military manpower, and direct revenue. This mastery of the contado anchors our legitimacy among the landed classes and extends our reach into every corner of the land we claim to rule.

We shall commission the Catasto — the most comprehensive survey of wealth and property undertaken by any government in medieval Europe, mapping the taxable assets of every citizen and household from the wealthiest merchant to the humblest artisan. By laying bare the full extent of our fiscal base, the Catasto allows us to distribute the burden of taxation with unprecedented fairness, replacing the factional manipulation of the old system with transparent and enforceable assessments. This reform earns the trust of our subjects, eases the cost of governing, and establishes a standard of administrative precision that future rulers of Tuscany will build upon.

We open our principal harbor to merchants of every faith and nation — Armenians, Jews, Greeks, and Flemings all welcomed without the religious conditions that other Mediterranean ports impose. This freedom draws skilled traders and financiers whose settlement enriches our city and swells our trade routes with goods that more closed ports cannot handle. Our cosmopolitan harbor grows from a modest coastal port into one of the most dynamic commercial centers in the western Mediterranean, drawing population and capital to our shores.

Our commissioning of the Uffizi as the administrative heart of our new Grand Duchy creates not merely a seat of government, but a stage for our power — its long corridor soon to be lined with antiquities, sculptures, and canvases that announce our ruler's dynasty's mastery of both statecraft and beauty. Across the city, we are establishing a secret workshop in the Palazzo Vecchio, where alchemists and craftsmen perfect a soft-paste porcelain — the first produced in Europe, rivalling the precious wares imported at great expense from China. These twin achievements of administration and artisanal ambition mark the apex of our patronage, announcing to every court in Christendom that Tuscany under the Grand Dukes is as much a center of refinement as of power.

Our Grand Duke has established the Accademia del Cimento — the Academy of Experiment — gathering the finest scientific minds of the age under a single roof devoted to empirical inquiry, its members bound by the motto Provando e Riprovando — testing and retesting — that sets a new standard for the pursuit of knowledge. At the same time, the Grand Duchy is reshaping the municipalities of Tuscany, replacing the patchwork of local privileges with uniform administrative procedures that make the state's authority felt in every town and valley. This combination of scientific ambition and administrative rigor defines our duchy as a state where both ideas and governance are held to the same exacting standard of proof.

Our ruler governs Tuscany by the principles of the Physiocrates, which state that land and agriculture are the true sources of all wealth. We will abolish serfdom and guild monopolies, work to free the grain trade from state controls, and will be reorganizing taxation around soil productivity rather than the privileges of merchants and nobles. This same spirit of rational governance is restructuring our commercial culture, dismantling the internal barriers that previously restricted the movement of goods and opening our markets to trade that guild charters had long excluded. This comprehensive reform of land and commerce is transforming Tuscany into a model of Enlightened administration, an experiment in rational governance that observers across Europe come to study and imitate.

items.name: Ulster
items.desc: At the heart of the … world and one of the traditional Cúige, the Five Provinces of …, Ulster has a unique presence in the world. But our people yearn to do and be more than we already are, and as such, the time has come for Ulster to assert itself as a major player on the world stage.
